events.summary: Skeletons Out of the Closet The annual Spooky Art Show returns to Lavaun's Community Gallery for its third year, this time as “Skeleton's Out of the Closet.” Curated from an open call for submissions, this show features art that is spooky, scary, strange, and out of the ordinary. Alberta Street Gallery member Julia Alora, a lifetime lover of Halloween, has hand-picked this year’s collection of frights and delights from more than 10 local artists. What makes art spooky? Art that focuses on fears, phobias, or disquieting themes. Settings or characters or creatures that are dark, born from night, or upsetting to see. Images that capture the fun and nostalgia of playing in a scary space through a safe lens, reminiscent of horror movies and Halloweens past. Come in for a thrill and a chill, find a new piece to haunt your home, and enjoy beautiful works of art perfect for those who are strange and unusual. Alberta Street Gallery is a friendly and vibrant cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.
events.title: Skeletons Out of the Closet: A Spooky Art Show

events.summary: The Chronic Pain Project is holding its next exhibition in the Aubrey R. Watzek Library at Lewis & Clark College! CPP showcases art by anyone with experiences relating to chronic pain. Some of our artists have created for decades, and others have only just begun. Through art, these artists make visible what millions live with but few understand. This exhibition asks us to consider what embodiment means while living with an invisible condition. CPP seeks to shift dominant narratives, educate the broader public, and create community. What does embodiment mean to you? We invite you to consider our theme as you peruse "Embodied Existence."
events.title: Embodied Existence

events.summary: ADX Fest is a new region-wide art and design festival activating venues, studios, and spaces across the Portland metro area. Throughout October 2026, ADX Fest celebrates the independent artists, designers, makers, and creatives powering our cultural and economic vitality. Over one dozen ADX Fest shows, workshops and classes take place in the Central Eastside at Art Design Xchange (ADX), 417 SE 11th Ave. ADX is accessible by TriMet, Portland Streetcar, and bike. Additional collaborations occur at 20+ independent venues, classrooms, makerspaces, and shops throughout the Portland region. ADX Fest is all throughout the month of October. We kick off October 2 with a grand opening party/First Friday shindig celebrating 15 years of making for Art Design Xchange. After that, check our calendar for dozens of creative events from St Johns to Multnomah Village.Creatives are the economic engine for Portland. From fine furniture, screenprinting, poetry, filmmaking, fine art, dance and stop motion animation to graphic design, photography, cartoon arts, music gear, home furnishings, beauty products and more, Portland IS the creative capital of THE UNIVERSE! And….We want to party about it! With you! ADX stands for Art Design Xchange, a woman owned- and operated- creative collective celebrating 15 years in the Buckman neighborhood. Check our event calendar and discover a new creative experience in your neighborhood. We are Community Powered + Created!

events.summary: Altan is celebrating forty years on the road, bringing their native music to world-renowned stages such as Carnagie Hall, the Sydney Opera House, Dublin's National Concert Hall as well as to the famous Glastonbury Festival, Tradfest Temple Bar in Dublin, and Festival Interceltique de Lorient in Brittany. Building on this history, their latest album 'Donegal' was released in 2024 \(Compass Records\) and has received widespread positive reviews. Altan has long been at the forefront of traditional Irish music, blending the raw energy of their native Donegal-fiddle style with a rare, melodic sensibility. events.summary: PDX CONTEMPORARY ART is pleased to present Soñé Que Revelabas, a solo exhibition of new work by photographer Georgina Reskala. The works in the exhibition center on a dream the artist had last year in which she approached her late sister, who whispered to her “Soñé que revelabas” or “I dreamed that you revealed.” Revelar in Spanish means to manifest or make public something that was secret or unknown, and is also the chemical process in photography by which a latent image becomes visible. She awoke trying to make sense of this message and wrote the sentence on a piece of paper on her studio wall. As the days and months went by, Reskala realized that she was still trying to make sense of the loss of her sister. Loss of language, interactions, moments, and memories that become fainter as a result of distance and time. This body of work became a personal account of the process of translation, not just in language, but of sounds, inflections, stories, memories, and dreams. Working with silver gelatin prints and photographs printed on textile, Reskala explores this estrangement that comes with the inability to fully translate from one language to another. Using a variety of printing techniques, she repeatedly alters her images, adding and redacting information through material processes of physically manipulating the paper, unthreading the warp and weft of the linen, and by printing, rephotographing, and reprinting the same image multiple times.
events.title: Georgina Reskala ·

Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: PDX CONTEMPORARY ART is pleased to present Soñé Que Revelabas, a solo exhibition of new work by photographer Georgina Reskala. The works in the exhibition center on a dream the artist had last year in which she approached her late sister, who whispered to her “Soñé que revelabas” or “I dreamed that you revealed.” Revelar in Spanish means to manifest or make public something that was secret or unknown, and is also the chemical process in photography by which a latent image becomes visible. She awoke trying to make sense of this message and wrote the sentence on a piece of paper on her studio wall. As the days and months went by, Reskala realized that she was still trying to make sense of the loss of her sister. Loss of language, interactions, moments, and memories that become fainter as a result of distance and time. This body of work became a personal account of the process of translation, not just in language, but of sounds, inflections, stories, memories, and dreams. Working with silver gelatin prints and photographs printed on textile, Reskala explores this estrangement that comes with the inability to fully translate from one language to another. Using a variety of printing techniques, she repeatedly alters her images, adding and redacting information through material processes of physically manipulating the paper, unthreading the warp and weft of the linen, and by printing, rephotographing, and reprinting the same image multiple times.
events.title: Georgina Reskala ·

events.summary: Lookout Landscape is an immersive art exhibition by Oregon-based artist and designer David Buckley Borden and a team of collaborators working across forestry, design, and engineering. Inspired by fire lookout towers, trail culture, and backcountry gear, the exhibition invites visitors onto a fabricated “Lookout Trail,” where a series of imaginative scenes—from a trailhead to a weather station, campground, and tool shed—reimagine the visual language of forestry and outdoor culture in the Pacific Northwest. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. events.summary: This former Southern Pacific Railroad station, fondly called the Old Train Station \(OTS\), is home to Friends of Historic Forest Grove. The Old Train Station now serves as a museum highlighting about 150 years of local history, from photographs and maps to clothing and furniture. It also houses an historic library and research center. Built in 1913, the station handled passenger and light freight service into 1929. After that only light freight came through. Burlingham and Sons purchased the building as office space for their seed company. Unfortunately, over the years this building has gone through some internal and external changes but some of the original station remains and can easy be found. events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Skeletons Out of the Closet The annual Spooky Art Show returns to Lavaun's Community Gallery for its third year, this time as “Skeleton's Out of the Closet.” Curated from an open call for submissions, this show features art that is spooky, scary, strange, and out of the ordinary. Alberta Street Gallery member Julia Alora, a lifetime lover of Halloween, has hand-picked this year’s collection of frights and delights from more than 10 local artists. What makes art spooky? Art that focuses on fears, phobias, or disquieting themes. Settings or characters or creatures that are dark, born from night, or upsetting to see. Images that capture the fun and nostalgia of playing in a scary space through a safe lens, reminiscent of horror movies and Halloweens past. Come in for a thrill and a chill, find a new piece to haunt your home, and enjoy beautiful works of art perfect for those who are strange and unusual. Alberta Street Gallery is a friendly and vibrant cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.
events.title: Skeletons Out of the Closet: A Spooky Art Show

events.summary: 'Cycles in the Infinite Dream' out July 24 on Sargent House Over the last decade, Chicago quartet REZN have carved out a unique place in the landscape of heavy music, chiseling away at the crude formations of the topography, mining the most concentrated metallic ore from the dirt, and shaping it all into something monumental, imposing, and divine. While REZN has always fused seismic riffs with effortless beauty and grandeur, their shifting strategies for wielding that polarity have involved varied compositional and stylistic decisions, most notably the light-and-dark contrast of companion albums Solace \(2023\) and Burden \(2024\). But with their newest full-length offering, Cycles in the Infinite Dream, REZN masterfully harness the oppressive weight of their full sonic armory to celestial melodies and sublime synesthesia-inducing atmospherics in a manner so seamless it feels otherworldly, as if occupying a liminal space between two realities.

events.summary: PDX CONTEMPORARY ART is pleased to present Soñé Que Revelabas, a solo exhibition of new work by photographer Georgina Reskala. The works in the exhibition center on a dream the artist had last year in which she approached her late sister, who whispered to her “Soñé que revelabas” or “I dreamed that you revealed.” Revelar in Spanish means to manifest or make public something that was secret or unknown, and is also the chemical process in photography by which a latent image becomes visible. She awoke trying to make sense of this message and wrote the sentence on a piece of paper on her studio wall. As the days and months went by, Reskala realized that she was still trying to make sense of the loss of her sister. Loss of language, interactions, moments, and memories that become fainter as a result of distance and time. This body of work became a personal account of the process of translation, not just in language, but of sounds, inflections, stories, memories, and dreams. Working with silver gelatin prints and photographs printed on textile, Reskala explores this estrangement that comes with the inability to fully translate from one language to another. Using a variety of printing techniques, she repeatedly alters her images, adding and redacting information through material processes of physically manipulating the paper, unthreading the warp and weft of the linen, and by printing, rephotographing, and reprinting the same image multiple times.
events.title: Georgina Reskala ·

Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

Eddie Soloway is a photographer, teacher, and storyteller committed to opening our eyes to the natural world. He has taught photography and creativity for leading photographic institutions and schools around the world. The Santa Fe Center for Photographic Arts \(now CENTER\) awarded Eddie the Excellence in Photographic Teaching Award, and Photo District News named Eddie one of America’s best photography workshop teachers. He divides his time between speaking on photography and creativity, teaching for leading photographic institutions, making fine-art prints, and publishing photographic projects. Eddie is the founder of the creative online gathering, Taproot. He is the author of the book, One Thousand Moons, the SEE THINK DO photo cards, and the Expressive Landscape video series. Eddie’s photography may be seen at www.eddiesoloway.com, hisworkshops and teaching materials at www.anaturaleye.com, and hiswriting at substack.com/@eddiesoloway.

events.summary: Hillsboro is a growing and diverse community, and people need different kinds of homes at different prices and stages of life. The Housing Options Project will look at how the City’s rules can make it easier to build more housing choices in Hillsboro. Over the next several years, the project will update the City’s housing rules to support construction of more homes, including apartments, townhomes, plexes, and accessory dwelling units \(ADUs\). events.summary: Liverpool Legends are four world-class musicians and actors, personally curated by the late Louise Harrison, sister of George Harrison, to honor her brother's legacy and faithfully recreate the band that changed the world forever. This Grammy-nominated, one-of-a-kind show features video narration created by Louise Harrison and traces the extraordinary musical evolution of The Beatles, from their early chart-topping hits through their groundbreaking psychedelic and studio years. Liverpool Legends have toured internationally with sold-out performances across the United States, Europe, Mexico, Canada, Israel, Ukraine, India, and South America. Career highlights include appearances at legendary venues such as the Cavern Club in Liverpool, Carnegie Hall, and the Rose Bowl, where they performed for more than 50,000 fans. The band has also recorded at the iconic Abbey Road Studios in London and received a Grammy nomination for their work on Fab Fan Memories: The Beatles Bond. With note-perfect vocals, meticulous attention to musical detail, authentic costume changes, vintage instruments, and stunning state-of-the-art multimedia, Liverpool Legends deliver an unforgettable live concert that allows audiences to experience the music, spirit, and legacy of The Beatles like never before.

events.summary: “Golden Shoals bridge the sometimes distant worlds of traditional bluegrass and old time music together. With one foot steeped in tradition and the other focused on fresh songwriting, Golden Shoals are helping to further the narrative of American Roots music and introducing the traditions of our past to a whole new generation of listeners.” - Kris Truelsen, WBCM Radio Bristol Golden Shoals is a fiddle and guitar duo with a "rousing old-time-style music that’s fueled by acerbic modern-day wit” \(-No Depression Magazine\). They are no strangers to traditional music, having placed in contests including Clifftop \(3rd place 2023, 4th place 2022\), Mount Airy, The Grand Masters Fiddlers Championship and Galax. Often switching instruments between fiddle, two guitars, and banjo, their original songs have been compared to Gillian Welch, with the added edge of instrumental prowess informed by energetic old time and bluegrass recordings. Initially brought together by a mutual love of American folk music, Golden Shoals' sound has expanded to include country, Americana, Indie and Experimental influences, allowing them to move more freely beyond genre boundaries with their songwriting while still emanating a deep understanding of Old-Time and Bluegrass music. Ever inspired by the enduring spirit of traditional Appalachian mountain music, their songwriting comes across as simple, honest, and fresh to the ears. The listener can expect the polished technique of conservatory training, in tandem with the grit, drive, and soul of musicians like Roscoe Holcomb or Ola Belle Reed.
events.title: Golden Shoals

events.summary: Reduce your social anxiety. Increase your confidence. Learn to navigate the world. Begin changing your psychology. Our newest class series isn't therapy, but it is incredibly therapeutic. We'll leverage the power of applied \(or process\) improvisation to bring the tools of improv to our daily lives. We'll anchor much of our work in the teachings & approaches of Augusto Boal and Paulo Friere, two educators who helped bring this style of improvisation to the world. Together, we'll learn how to: 🗣️ Share our most powerful life stories with honesty & vulnerability 💥 Explore those stories with creativity & support 👁️ See & experience our lives through the lens of others 💪🏼 Discover our psychological strengths and, most importantly... ❤️ Evolve our relationships through the power of insight 🗣️ 1:1 Sessions Included The practice of applied improvisation is fun, but also requires vulnerability. For this reason, this series includes a 30-60min 1:1 session with your teacher. In these virtual sessions, we'll discuss and celebrate your breakthroughs and then examine the patterns that have emerged from your work that might be holding you back from even deeper successes.
events.title: Improv for Personal Development | Support for anxiety & depression

events.summary: Poor Man’s Whiskey presents a special two set evening of original music, and a second set of their world acclaimed “Dark Side of the Moonshine” (a bluegrass interpretation of the classic Pink Floyd album). The set is an interactive experience with a Wizard of Oz theme. Audiences are encouraged to come dressed as your favorite Wizard of Oz character. Prizes go to best costumes! Poor Man’s Whiskey is an Americana band originating in the San Francisco area in 2001. The music is rooted around the songwriting talents of Josh Brough and Jason Beard (who met in 1993 at the University of California, Santa Barbara). Poor Man’s Whiskey’s live show and sound is a blend of high octane old time/bluegrass music (often done on traditional acoustic instruments of banjo, guitar, fiddle, and mandolin) and a more psychedelic blues/jam rock style that calls upon their earlier influences such as Pink Floyd, Allman Brothers Band, and the Grateful Dead. Poor Man’s Whiskey seamlessly transitions between acoustic and electric styles with a carefully crafted commitment that revolves around well written songs and stories...while maintaining an exciting element of improvisation and the openness to let a song expand.

events.summary: Soul-tronic dance-pop Moody, bass-driven soul/pop with an undeniable edge. Portland natives Jenni and Amanda Price-twin sisters with an unbreakable musical bond-create a sound that's equal parts timeless and distinctly their own. From the moment they open their mouths, you're hooked. Their vocals are rich and soaring, effortlessly blending harmonies that feel both raw and ethereal. With songwriting that taps into the deepest parts of the human experience, their music resonates long after the last note. Joined by longtime collaborators Aaron Altemose and Josh Lorenzen, the band has spent over 15 years fine-tuning their signature sound-one that blends elements of soul, pop, rock, and edm into something that's unpredictable yet undeniable. The production is layered with rich textures and sonic surprises that keep you coming back for more. Their music is more than just melodies-it's an emotional journey. Each track is heart-wrenching and soul-stirring, urging you to feel, to think, and to act. It's the kind of music that doesn't just soundtrack your life-it challenges it. With a powerful presence and a sound that defies easy categorization, Jenni, Amanda, Aaron, and Josh have crafted a collection of songs that are impossible to ignore. Website: http://www.theammusic.com Soundcloud: http://www.soundcloud.com/acousticmindsmusicds Facebook: http://www.facebook.com/acousticmindsmusic - All ages welcome

events.summary: Rock, Revolution. *LIZZIE* Brings America's Favorite Murder Mystery to Portland Marin Summer Theater and Bridgetown Conservatory of Musical Theatre present *LIZZIE* Music by Steven Cheslik-deMeyer, Alan Stevens Hewitt & Tim Maner Book and Lyrics by Tim Maner & Steven Cheslik-deMeyer What really happened inside the Borden house? Based on the historical events surrounding the 1892 murders of Andrew and Abby Borden, LIZZIE explores the days leading up to the shocking crime through the eyes of four women (Voni Kengla as Lizzie Borden, Jessica Tidd as Emma Borden, Tia Lempert as Alice Russell, and Ashley Moore as Bridget Sullivan), determined to tell their own story. With a thunderous rock score inspired by artists such as Heart, The Runaways, and Bikini Kill, the musical is a bold examination of abuse, repression, freedom, and rage. The show has earned international acclaim, with productions in more than 100 theaters across 11 countries and multiple Best Musical awards. More information and tickets can be found at https:\\\\lizziepdx.com.

events.summary: Our audiences have been asking us to bring back the Halloween show for years…. Be careful what you wish for. Stephen Mallatratt’s The Woman in Black has been terrifying audiences since its London debut in 1987 and is one of the most successful and terrifying shows in West End history. Based on Susan Hill’s beloved novel, it’s one of the most celebrated ghost stories ever staged: atmospheric, relentless, and the kind of theatrical experience that makes you question every shadow on your way to the car. Set in a remote English village, it follows a young lawyer unraveling the secrets of a recently deceased client and the vengeful presence that doesn’t want him to. Just two actors portray all the characters, leaning into what B&B’s performers do best. Chilling, clever, and unforgettable. Halloween is back at Bag&Baggage…and we brought something with us. events.summary: "Marigolds y Memorias" is an original devised production inspired by the traveling carpa tradition, in which humor, music, and storytelling come together in a vibrant theatrical journey. Guided by an elder, a younger generation learns to build an altar, the heart of Día de Muertos, discovering the meaning behind each of its elements, from candles and marigolds to photographs, ofrendas, and cherished recuerdos. Through song, dance, and short theatrical vignettes, the altar gradually takes shape as an act of remembrance and cultural inheritance, inviting audiences to consider how traditions are taught, how memory is kept alive, and what is carried forward when we share rituals across generations. Age Recommendation: All Ages Estimated Running Time: 1 hour 30 minutes, including one intermission
events.title: Marigolds y Memorias

events.summary: Glass. Kill. Bluebeard. Imp. is a collection of four short, surreal plays by acclaimed English playwright, Caryl Churchill. Premiering at London's Royal Court Theatre in 2019, these darkly imaginative works weave together myth, fairy tale, and contemporary horror. Moving between collective voices and intimate encounters, Churchill explores violence, power, desire, and the stories we tell to make sense of a fractured world. By turns funny, haunting, and unsettling, the plays invite audiences into a landscape where the familiar becomes strange and ancient myths reveal modern anxieties without explanation or comfort. A girl made of glass. Gods and murders. A serial killer's friends. And a secret in a bottle.​ Four short plays by Caryl Churchill Directed by Samantha Van Der Merwe​October 10th - November 7th 2026

events.summary: ETANASoul'd Out Presents: ETANA with special guests TBA Doors: 7:00pm Show: 8:00pm Ages 21\+ welcome. https://etanamusic.com/ Singer, songwriter, and humanitarian Etana is a powerhouse vocalist and 2X Grammy Award nominee. Its a been over a decade after her debut as a reggae artist, she is now a recognized and respected entertainer in her native Jamaica and is also well known worldwide. Born Shauna McKenzie, the young talent migrated to the United States for the opportunity and briefly pursued a pop music career before rediscovering her roots as an adult and adopting the moniker Etana, , "rdquo" -\> The Strong One" in Swahili. The return home spurred the evolution of her sound and is evident in her body of work expressed as the fusion of folk, soul, jazz, and reggae. Etana taps into the likes of Marcia Griffiths, Etta James, and Miriam Makeba for harnessing a deeply emotional sound, and she is the modern embodiment of their influence. In 2008 Etana debuted the album, The Strong One, featuring various musicians and producers. The project reached the \#12 spot on the Reggae Billboard chart, and consecutively released singles released by VP Records, which helped to introduce the spirited singer to the world. Lyrical hits , "rdquo" -\> Warrior Love" and , "rdquo" -\> I Am Not Afraid" made a lasting impression, as did , "rdquo" -\> Free" and , "rdquo" -\> Happy Heart" from the second album Free Expressions, notably a repeat Reggae Billboard chart climber. Not to be outdone, she released her fourth album I Rise to much acclaim, nabbing the \#1 spot on the iconic chart, marking the first female artist out of Jamaica to earn such a designation seventeen years. Fast forward to 2018, Etana was nominated for the 61st Annual Grammy Awards for Reggae Forever in the Best Reggae Album category. The project was co-produced by Etana \(Freemind Music\) and distributed by Tad's Records. The distinction by The Recording Academy marked the first time in over twenty years that a woman was designated that bracket. In 2019, she released the eight-track EP Dimensions, then a full-length album Gemini released in 2020, Her latest album Pamoja \(2021\) earned Etana her 2nd Grammy Nomination, the album features from Vybz Kartel, Damian Marley, and Stonebwoy.
events.title: ETANA

events.summary: TICKETS ️ truewest.info/DinoJr26 On Sale Now! ---------------------------------------- Finally! The sixth studio album Dinosaur Jr. have recorded in the 20 years since their triumphal rebirth. There have been several live and/or closet cleaning collections to keep us punters sated for the five years since Sweep It Into Space, but there is nothing quite like having a full slab of new Dino tunes to fry your ears. And There Near has all knobs set to Extra Crispy. Created in short, intense bursts over the course of a year at Amherst's Bisquiteen Studio, There Near was recorded almost entirely by Dino's core trio -- king of the thunder tubs, Murph, human tornado Lou Barlow on bass/vocals and the inimitable J Mascis on guitar/vocals -- with a bit of piano and organ work by local master musician, Ken Mauri. And the album roars from start to finish. Trying to define the essence of Dino's sound is never easy. It's an instantly recognizable blend of loose vocals, sharp guitars and an animalistic rhythm section, but these parts combine into a whole far more magical and exciting than its components. In strict rock-write terms, you might call the approach “post-core power balladeering,” but what use is that? Dinosaur Jr. invented their formula for noise/pop jiggering around the same time Husker Dü were trying out some of the same ideas, all of which got made popular by a band they inspired called Nirvana. But that's an old and much-told tale. J's guitar tone throughout There Near is even more animalistic than usual, perhaps owing partly to the fact he's playing through a recently acquired 70's Mesa Boogie MK 1 amp. “I bought the same amp that Chris Dixon had when we made our first album,” J says. “Chris recorded us at his house with his amp. It has a real interesting sound I haven't gotten for a while. And it's something I was trying to get back to on this album. The Stones started using Mesa Boogies in the '70s after they heard Santana playing through them. Then The Clash copied The Stones, etc. As the years went on into the MK 2 and so on, the Boogie got more metal sounding. But the MK 1 has a souped-up Fender sound. You always hear how Rick Rubin always makes bands he's producing sit down and listen to their first album and say let's get back to that sound. So I just gave myself his advice." Asked about the philosophical opacity of his lyrical approach, J says. “I'm not always sure what a song is 'about' when I'm writing it. I guess the meaning will present itself at some point. I'll use whatever words work. And a lot of it will be influenced by whatever esoteric mumbo jumbo I'm reading at the time. I try not to think too hard about any of it. I think it's a drag that Spotify shows all the lyrics to a song. What's the fun of that? Japanese labels always wanted us to give them lyrics to print. I wouldn't hand them over so they'd just have to try and figure them out. It has always been better to make up your own version of lyrics to songs by the Stones or R.E.M. or whoever. I mean, R.E.M.'s whole thing was about mumbling. I never understood why they caved to pressure and started enunciating." “Someone suggested this album sounds more upbeat, but I guess that's to do with my delivery, because lyrics like 'No Friends' might make you think otherwise. But I usually write in the third person. It's all just make believe.”

events.summary: PDX CONTEMPORARY ART is pleased to present Soñé Que Revelabas, a solo exhibition of new work by photographer Georgina Reskala. The works in the exhibition center on a dream the artist had last year in which she approached her late sister, who whispered to her “Soñé que revelabas” or “I dreamed that you revealed.” Revelar in Spanish means to manifest or make public something that was secret or unknown, and is also the chemical process in photography by which a latent image becomes visible. She awoke trying to make sense of this message and wrote the sentence on a piece of paper on her studio wall. As the days and months went by, Reskala realized that she was still trying to make sense of the loss of her sister. Loss of language, interactions, moments, and memories that become fainter as a result of distance and time. This body of work became a personal account of the process of translation, not just in language, but of sounds, inflections, stories, memories, and dreams. Working with silver gelatin prints and photographs printed on textile, Reskala explores this estrangement that comes with the inability to fully translate from one language to another. Using a variety of printing techniques, she repeatedly alters her images, adding and redacting information through material processes of physically manipulating the paper, unthreading the warp and weft of the linen, and by printing, rephotographing, and reprinting the same image multiple times.
events.title: Georgina Reskala ·

events.summary: Lookout Landscape is an immersive art exhibition by Oregon-based artist and designer David Buckley Borden and a team of collaborators working across forestry, design, and engineering. Inspired by fire lookout towers, trail culture, and backcountry gear, the exhibition invites visitors onto a fabricated “Lookout Trail,” where a series of imaginative scenes—from a trailhead to a weather station, campground, and tool shed—reimagine the visual language of forestry and outdoor culture in the Pacific Northwest. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. Plan your visit and explore the exhibition: worldforestry.org/lookout-landscape

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: This exhibition highlights a distinct artistic collaboration between printmakers Cassie Ferguson and Charlie Cohan, marking the creative intersection of their independent yet interrelated studios, Lost Bearings Press (LBP) and BurnPrint Studio (BPS). Centered on a shared dedication to traditional printmaking, the showcase features a diverse range of techniques, including stone lithography, screen printing, polyester plate lithography, and relief printmaking. The conceptual foundation of this exhibition hinges on a collaborative print created by Cohan and Ferguson in 2017, which juxtaposed the iconic Burnside Skatepark with an urban overpass. This visual conversation continues in Ferguson’s ongoing series of stone lithographs capturing DIY skateparks. Her work seeks to honor and archive the subcultural spaces that have shaped her lived experience. Because these grassroots spaces often thrive under overpasses and within neglected industrial zones, her prints seamlessly connect with Cohan’s imagery of Portland’s monumental bridges. Together, the artists offer a multifaceted view of the city, championing the gritty beauty of structural environments. Their works invite viewers to reflect on their own relationship to the municipal landscape and to find new ways of seeing everyday urban scenes. Additionally, the exhibition introduces recent work by Nakemiah “Kiki” Williams, produced in collaboration with Ferguson and Cohan at LBP and BPS. This project marks the debut publication for LBP and brings their history full circle, as both Williams and Ferguson are alumnae of Cohan’s printmaking program at the University of Hawai’i at Mānoa. This collaboration marks the beginning of collaborative print work at LBP, which is now open for publishing and contracted prints of primarily stone lithographs.
events.title: Under the Overpass

events.summary: Chefas Projects is pleased to present Outside Nature, an exhibition of paintings and works by Kristen Diederich, on view October 23 through November 21, 2026. The exhibition opens with a reception on Friday, October 23, from 5 to 8 PM. Working across painting, sculpture, and poetry, Diederich explores the complex relationship between human desire and the natural world. Through luminous, layered landscapes characterized by cinematic depth, chromatic intensity, and intuitive mark-making, her work considers how nature is framed, interpreted, and shaped by human intervention, and what resists those efforts at control. At the heart of Diederich’s practice is an ongoing poem written in tandem with her visual work over the past decade. Rather than presenting the poem as a separate text, Diederich releases it line by line through the titles of her paintings, creating an evolving dialogue between language and image. Each work becomes part of a larger narrative, one that remains open to shifting interpretations and associations. In Outside Nature, Diederich draws on the symbolism, materiality, and visual language of the late Gothic Unicorn Tapestries, housed at The Met Cloisters in New York. These intricate works depict the Hortus Conclusus, or enclosed garden - a space defined by boundaries, desire, and the relationship between the cultivated and the wild. Within the tapestries, plants appear in perpetual bloom or fruit, transcending their natural seasons and geographic origins. Their imagined abundance raises questions about how nature is represented, ordered, and transformed through human vision. Diederich considers the garden not simply as an ornamental space, but as a site of rhetoric and exclusion. The word garden is connected to the idea of a boundary in many cultures, suggesting that cultivation is as much an expression of human desire as it is a gathering of living species. What is permitted to flourish, what is left outside, and what remains unseen become equally significant. Nature, in Diederich’s view, cannot be reduced to decoration; flora and fauna follow their own timescales and patterns, often exceeding the systems imposed upon them. The tapestries also offer a point of departure for Diederich’s investigation into repetition, perception, and the mysterious life of images. Their intricate stitching and distinctive colors, historically produced through dyes such as weld, madder, and woad, reveal a world in which no two marks are quite the same. As Diederich writes, “repetition does not exist.” A flower may appear to be the same as another, yet each instance of blooming carries its own temporal and material difference. These ideas extend into broader questions about knowledge, technology, and transformation. Reflecting on the differences between human inquiry and the extraction of data through artificial intelligence, Diederich considers the ways we filter and alter our environments to create new possibilities for thought. The unicorn, a central figure in the tapestries, becomes a point of connection to alchemy and purification, suggesting the potential for transformation, of matter, perception, and the self. Throughout Outside Nature, images function as distillations of thought, memory, and experience. They resist singular meanings even as they generate narratives that can be felt and understood intuitively. By bringing together landscape, poetry, historical imagery, and material investigation, Diederich invites viewers to consider the unstable boundaries between nature and culture, representation and reality, and repetition and change. Kristen Diederich (b. 1994, Tallahassee, Florida) works across painting, sculpture, and poetry. She works from Whitehead Island off the coast of Maine and from her studio in Northeast Portland, Oregon.
events.title: KRISTEN DIEDERICH | OUTSIDE NATURE

events.summary: *My Omaha* Film Screening & Conversation When: Fri, Oct 23, 6:00 pm (doors open at 5:30 pm) | Where: FPC Chapel What does it take to stay connected when our deepest beliefs pull us apart? My Omaha is a documentary following filmmaker Nick Beaulieu as he returns to Omaha to document the city’s racial justice movement while reconnecting with his terminally ill, conservative father. Through his relationship with community organizer Leo Louis II, Nick confronts a side of his hometown—and himself—that he had not fully seen. The documentary premieres October 5 on PBS’s Independent Lens. On Friday, October 23, First Presbyterian Church of Portland's Service Beyond Our Walls committee invites the congregation, downtown neighbors, students, and the wider Portland community to gather in the FPC Chapel to watch the film together. At a time when political and social divisions can make honest conversation difficult, My Omaha asks what it means to tell the truth about injustice, listen across deep disagreement, and remain in relationship when convictions pull us apart. After the 85-minute film, Nick and Leo will join us live for a conversation with the audience. Watch the trailer for the film by clicking here! Admission is free but RSVPs are appreciated at https://www.eventbrite.com/e/my-omaha-film-screening-converstion-tickets-2002887850477?aff=oddtdtcreator Free parking will be available in our underground garage on 12th.
events.title: My Omaha Film Screening & Conversation

events.summary: We Built You a Garden is the third installment of Metro’s Community Voices project, a multimedia storytelling initiative that invites residents of Metro Affordable Housing Bond-funded communities to explore the meaning of home through photography, writing and collective reflection. Hosted through a summer workshop series at the Strong Empowerment Village in partnership with artists Gwen Hoeffgen and Domenic Toliver, the project centers the experiences of residents with ties to North and Northeast Portland. Through weekly workshops and the use of film photography and creative writing, participants documented places, people and memories that shape their understanding of home, legacy and belonging. Their work considers displacement, resilience and community history, creating a powerful collection of stories that honor the past while imagining what can continue to grow. Ultimately, We Built You a Garden asks what’s been inherited, what’s been built, and what we want to leave growing for the next generation. It speaks to the ongoing impact of displacement in Portland for the Black community, but it also affirms what it took — and continues to take — to nourish, tend and build home. Exhibition and events: Free admission Oct. 9, 5:30pm to 8pm: We Built You a Garden | Exhibition Opening at The BLACK Gallery Join us for the opening of We Built You a Garden, with remarks and refreshments as well as free copies of the project’s publication. Open to public with remarks from Metro, artists, and Don’t Shoot PDX . Oct. 23, 6pm to 8pm: We Built You a Garden | Community Conversation at The BLACK Gallery A conversation about the past, present, and future of Portland through the experiences of the people who live, work, organize, and build here. Artists, activists, community members, youth and Metro come together to consider what we have inherited, what we have built, what is changing, and what we want to leave growing for the next generation. The BLACK Gallery will be open to the public on the following Sundays from 1pm to 4pm during the exhibition’s display: Oct. 11, Oct. 18, Oct. 25 and Nov. 1.
events.title: We Built You a Garden

events.summary: Frameline50 — Audience Award, Best Documentary Feature Provincetown International Film Festival — John Schlesinger Award for Best Documentary Director RiverRun International Film Festival — Best Documentary Feature Every Christmas, cowboys, families and returning migrants gather in Michoacán for the jaripeo, a traditional Mexican rodeo steeped in ritual, spectacle and machismo. But just beyond the arena, another story is unfolding. In fleeting touches, knowing glances and secret encounters, queer desire finds its own place within this deeply rooted tradition. Filmmakers Efraín Mojica and Rebecca Zweig take us inside this world with extraordinary intimacy, weaving raw vérité, Super 8 and dreamlike memory into a sensual portrait of queer life, rural Mexico and the complicated pull of home. At once tender, sexy and visually intoxicating, Jaripeo finds beauty in contradiction and freedom in unexpected places, revealing queerness not outside tradition, but alive within it. OPENING NIGHT IS KINDLY SPONSORED BY STACEY BANAHAN, BRIAN CARR & THOMAS LAPIERRE

events.summary: The year is 2056. We always knew they were out there…we just didn’t know they would attack so soon. Our city has fallen. Alien invaders and their cyborg forces have reduced the streets to rubble, and the few remaining survivors are doing whatever they can to escape. As if that weren’t enough, the destruction has brought another threat out of the shadows: zombies. This year’s interactive, no-contact haunted theatre drops you into the middle of the invasion. Choose how you face the apocalypse: Join the Resistance Rent an optional laser-tag weapon \(\+$2\) and fight back. The equipment uses a safe, invisible infrared beam to activate designated targets and trigger special effects as you move through the theatre. Become a Refugee Prefer not to use laser tag? Make your way through the ruined city as a refugee, trying to escape with your life while danger waits around every corner. Apocalypse in the Grove may include fog, laser lighting, loud noises, strobe effects, simulated fire, cold sparks, sudden scares, and intense theatrical environments. Will you join the resistance—or simply try to survive? When you purchase a ticket, you purchase a reservation for a 30 minute window. You must arrive in this timeframe or your entry could be delayed or denied. There are 6 people in each tour of the haunted theatre. This experience is wheelchair accessible. Children 12 and under MUST be accompanied by an adult.

events.summary: Modern Biology has brought ‘plant music’ to the masses. Originally educated as a biologist, veteran musician Tarun Nayar brings his passion for nature and sound together in an ambient project that is organismic, immediate, uplifting, and deeply contextual. He uses modular synthesis, home built synthesizers and other analog equipment to improvise with the natural vibrations of a certain place and time - via plant bioelectricity, latent electromagnetic radiation, and even the earth's resonant hum. Trained from childhood in Indian classical music, he uses the system of Indian raga to mold his musical choices for time of day and season. His performances are an effort to bring the listener into the resent moment through vibration, space, and connection. Tarun is passionate about protecting wild places and has committed the lion's share of the proceeds of this project to supporting the natural world.
events.title: Modern Biology

events.summary: Opening for Alex Misko East Coast USA, Western Canada, & West Coast USA! "His live performance is a refreshing take on the solo Acoustic Guitar, alchemizing every part of the instrument for original compositions with elements of folk, world, blues, jazz, and post-rock, all anchored in his virtuosic mastery of fingerstyle technique inspired by Michael Hedges, Andy Mckee, and Antoine Dufour." Forest crafts a unique combination of fingerstyle, tapping and percussive playing that is all his own. Drawing from various influences like Michael Hedges, Andy Mckee, Antoine Dufour, Scale The Summit, Led Zeppelin, Chon, and Covet, each song is a musical journey that further shows what two hands and a guitar can accomplish. Underscoring these sonic adventures with an exciting, welcoming and humorous stage presence that exudes every ounce of passion he has for his craft. Although initially enamored by classic rock and heavy metal in his teenage years, his curiosity led to a focus on solo acoustic guitar in 2015. Upon discovering the nuances that a steel string acoustic guitar can create, he quickly found the home for his compositions. These joyful and adventurous music experiments have led him to performing both nationally and internationally, from California to North Carolina, All across Canada and even to Australia. The year 2018 saw the debut release of Forest’s debut instrumental album, “Let The Clouds Pass.”

events.summary: Rock, Revolution. *LIZZIE* Brings America's Favorite Murder Mystery to Portland Marin Summer Theater and Bridgetown Conservatory of Musical Theatre present *LIZZIE* Music by Steven Cheslik-deMeyer, Alan Stevens Hewitt & Tim Maner Book and Lyrics by Tim Maner & Steven Cheslik-deMeyer What really happened inside the Borden house? Based on the historical events surrounding the 1892 murders of Andrew and Abby Borden, LIZZIE explores the days leading up to the shocking crime through the eyes of four women (Voni Kengla as Lizzie Borden, Jessica Tidd as Emma Borden, Tia Lempert as Alice Russell, and Ashley Moore as Bridget Sullivan), determined to tell their own story. With a thunderous rock score inspired by artists such as Heart, The Runaways, and Bikini Kill, the musical is a bold examination of abuse, repression, freedom, and rage. The show has earned international acclaim, with productions in more than 100 theaters across 11 countries and multiple Best Musical awards. Nick Lucifer in Club Hell, performed by Sean Lujan (Design for Living, Salomé) and Blavatsky, performed by Anne Sorce (Nice People, Happyness). NICK LUCIFER IN CLUB HELL The story of the universe told by a weathered gangster in “Club Hell” located well down below. BLAVATSKY Madame Blavatsky welcomes you to her private inner quarters to witness truth, lies, psychic phenomena, chickens, monkeys, nonsense, foolishness and drivel. “I’ve always wondered how many great artists have never been recognized. I would venture many. “I believe Don Nigro was a genius of theatre you never heard of” says director Jerry Mouawad. After I selected four of his works earlier this year, Nigro died. The Flying Solo Festival, which features four of his solos, has now become a homage to Nigro’s prolific work - he wrote over 500 plays!” American Theatre’s Lawrence Harbison wrote “he was hardly on the radar. Why not? Don lived in a small house in Northeast Ohio with his father, a disabled veteran who had been seriously wounded in the Battle of the Bulge and needed constant care. So, Don couldn’t travel, making it hard for him to do the sort of networking so important for establishing a reputation. And, anyway, he would rather stay home and write.” Production Credits: *Light Design:* Ronnie Rantis Costume Design: Laura Helgeson Sound Design: Myrrh Larsen Note: For Mature Audiences

events.summary: At a time when many theatres are closing their doors or reducing programming, 100 Lives Repertory in Portland’s Buckman neighborhood is celebrating the inaugural season in its brand-new space. And the first play is a doozy: a sleek, sly, sci-fi mystery titled Anthropology, penned by Lauren Gunderson, one of America’s most produced playwrights. Anthropology is about a grieving computer coder, Merril, who builds an AI replica of her missing and presumed dead sister. Adding to the loss, Merril’s relationship with her girlfriend has come to an end, which draws her deeper and deeper into her ‘project’ of bringing back a version of her sister, to help heal her grief and lessen her loneliness. This is the Oregon premiere of Anthropology which had its world debut in London at Hampstead Theatre in 2023. The play runs Thursday through Sunday from October 23 through November 15. It features an all-female, four-actor cast and is directed by 100 Lives Rep’s Executive Director Cat Plein. Due to nudity and sexual situations, it is recommended only for adult audiences.

events.summary: Our audiences have been asking us to bring back the Halloween show for years…. Be careful what you wish for. Stephen Mallatratt’s The Woman in Black has been terrifying audiences since its London debut in 1987 and is one of the most successful and terrifying shows in West End history. Based on Susan Hill’s beloved novel, it’s one of the most celebrated ghost stories ever staged: atmospheric, relentless, and the kind of theatrical experience that makes you question every shadow on your way to the car. Set in a remote English village, it follows a young lawyer unraveling the secrets of a recently deceased client and the vengeful presence that doesn’t want him to. Just two actors portray all the characters, leaning into what B&B’s performers do best. Chilling, clever, and unforgettable. Halloween is back at Bag&Baggage…and we brought something with us. Show Dates: October 15 – November 1, 2026 Thu – Sat at 7:30pm, Sun at 2pm Special Dates: Thursday, October 15 is a preview performance, with discounted tickets. Friday, October 16, is Opening Night! Sat, Oct. 24th – ASL Interpreted Performance Sun, Oct. 25th – Audio Described Performance

events.summary: "Marigolds y Memorias" is an original devised production inspired by the traveling carpa tradition, in which humor, music, and storytelling come together in a vibrant theatrical journey. Guided by an elder, a younger generation learns to build an altar, the heart of Día de Muertos, discovering the meaning behind each of its elements, from candles and marigolds to photographs, ofrendas, and cherished recuerdos. Through song, dance, and short theatrical vignettes, the altar gradually takes shape as an act of remembrance and cultural inheritance, inviting audiences to consider how traditions are taught, how memory is kept alive, and what is carried forward when we share rituals across generations. Age Recommendation: All Ages Estimated Running Time: 1 hour 30 minutes, including one intermission
events.title: Marigolds y Memorias

events.summary: Night Flight’s Fright Night – A Halloween Circus returns to the historic Alberta Rose Theatre with a queer-gothic-circus spoof of the Phantom of the Opera! Join us for a night of high-flying camp, outrageous scandal, and breathtaking aerial acrobatics. Forget everything you thought you knew about the brooding genius in the mask. Our Phantom isn’t just hiding in the shadows—he’s swinging from the rafters, singing dramatically from the balcony, and desperately trying to seduce the lead baritone while sabotaging every heteronormative trope in sight. Featuring an extraordinary cast of world-class circus artists, this show serves up a wicked cocktail of high-flying danger, sultry gothic horror, and laugh-out-loud comedy. Expect spine-chilling ghostly acrobats on the trapeze, scandalous duets on aerial chains, and contortionists so flexible they make the Phantom’s mood swings look rigid. Will the Phantom win the heart of his muse? Will the diva get her wig on in time? Will the chandelier flatten the front row? Grab your tightest corset, slip into your most dramatic cape, and join us for the ultimate Halloween night out. Whether you’re a lifelong theater geek, a circus fanatic, or just a creature of the night looking for a wildly funny, jaw-dropping show, this year’s Fright Night promises a hauntingly glamorous evening you’ll never forget! Featuring Jack StockLynn of Sir Cupcake’s Queer Circus, Night Flight’s 2026 Fright Night is a Halloween tradition not to be missed! Tickets vanish faster than the Phantom in a puff of stage fog—secure yours before the opera house burns down!

events.summary: Experience soaring indie rock with Black Belt Eagle Scout, the acclaimed Swinomish/Iñupiaq songwriter and guitarist Katherine Paul. With richly textured guitar work and evocative vocals, she creates music that is a love letter to indigenous strength and healing. Blending indie rock, dream pop, shoegaze, and Pacific Northwest grunge with deeply personal songwriting and Indigenous musical influences, Black Belt Eagle Scout is known for dynamic live performances that travel from hushed moments of reflection to immersive waves of cathartic release. Praised by Pitchfork, NPR Music, and Rolling Stone for powerful albums, including The Land, The Water, The Sky, Paul’s music carries the spirit of the Pacific Northwest, of her ancestral lands. Drawing from themes of identity, community, resilience, and connection to place, she crafts a space where grief, joy, love, and resilience converge, celebrating and honoring all the ancestors who walked these lands before her.
events.title: Black Belt Eagle Scout

events.summary: Glass. Kill. Bluebeard. Imp. is a collection of four short, surreal plays by acclaimed English playwright, Caryl Churchill. Premiering at London's Royal Court Theatre in 2019, these darkly imaginative works weave together myth, fairy tale, and contemporary horror. Moving between collective voices and intimate encounters, Churchill explores violence, power, desire, and the stories we tell to make sense of a fractured world. By turns funny, haunting, and unsettling, the plays invite audiences into a landscape where the familiar becomes strange and ancient myths reveal modern anxieties without explanation or comfort. A girl made of glass. Gods and murders. A serial killer's friends. And a secret in a bottle.​ Four short plays by Caryl Churchill Directed by Samantha Van Der Merwe​October 10th - November 7th 2026
events.title: Glass. Kill. Bluebeard. Imp. by Caryl Churchill

events.summary: Will these stories stay behind glass, or will you open a door to the past? Something isn't right here. That book is out of place. There is a card in the display case, but no item behind it. There are antiques in the incorrect place; and artefacts that are standing wrong side up. Clearly, the venue needs your help. As curators of other nearby museums, you are called to the venue after hours in order to help figure out what is causing these disturbances. Once inside, you are greeted by one of the exhibits who has come to life. They are happy to show you around and share tales about the other exhibits. As you hear stories from their lives, it becomes clear that one of them is the culprit behind these disturbances. The question is, which one? Succeed and you will find yourself promoted. Fail, and you may find yourself trapped behind glass forever. Enter an immersive historic experience where exhibits come to life, and there’s a mystery for you to solve! Presented by Live History, a Governor General’s Award nominated international touring theatre company who produces site specific customizable mysteries around the world, and the Oswego Heritage Council.

events.summary: Gregory Uhlmann is a guitarist, composer, and producer from Chicago living in Los Angeles. His musical palette embraces beautiful warble-y sounds, low fuzzy vibrations, and playful rhythms that overlap in surprising ways. His often-otherworldly guitar tones and syncopated picking style are immediately recognizable across a vast array of musical collaborations, and that distinction while maintaining a shapeshifting flexibility is no small feat. Uhlmann’s early work as co-leader of LA indie experimental outfit Fell Runner established his presence on the West coast scene after relocating from Chicago, and his resume since includes stints as a regular recording/touring member of Perfume Genius, Hand Habits, and Anna Butterss’s backing band. Whether he’s contributing to the LA trance-jazz improvisation of SML, the progressive electro-acoustic chamber music of his trio with Josh Johnson and Sam Wilkes, or in the hushed melancholic rhythm machine of Duffy x Uhlmann \(his duo with Meg Duffy of Hand Habits\), it’s clear that Uhlmann is a lead asset in every collaboration. His work as a solo artist ranges from cleverly arranged chamber-folk songwriting to beautifully abstract experimental jazz-informed instrumental compositions, and his latest album, Extra Stars, explores that latter territory to a deeper degree than ever before. This new work, his solo debut for International Anthem, pulls Uhlmann even further into the spotlight while showcasing his knack for directing the talent of his community of collaborators, establishing him as one of the most exciting emergent artists in modern music.
events.title: Gregory Uhlmann & Resavoir

The beating heart of the Pacific Northwest’s GD community, the band’s ever-expanding fanbase is an experience unto themselves. Using the Dead’s repertoire as a springboard for limitless potential and improvisation, Garcia Birthday Band are a cornerstone of the modern Grateful Dead universe, and their fans have come to expect the unexpected as the norm. Placing no boundaries on eras of the Dead’s career or catalog, and drawing on decades of individual and shared experience, GBB play the music through an auditory kaleidoscope. Composed of some of the most ace players of the Oregon live music community, the band makes every show an act of exploration, both musically and spiritually. United hearts and minds blur the line between the stage and crowd – a carnival of human potential. events.summary: Born *Lucas Macfadden* in Hollywood, CA Cut Chemist has been recording and performing for nearly 30 years. Known as a turntablist, he started his journey into djing at age 11. By the time he was 14 year old, Cut started recording with his friends (including Chali 2na of Jurassic 5) in an inclosed sun patio that his dad converted into a small make-shift recording studio. By age 21, Cut was a founding member of both the rap group Jurassic 5 and the Grammy award winning Latin funk outfit, Ozomatli. His involvement with both groups helped develop a taste for music and rhythms from around the world while keeping his passion for the hip hop tradition. His mix-tapes and remixes became critically acclaimed. His ‘Chemist’ moniker was fully realized with his instrumental, Lesson 6: The Lecture. In the years following, Cut started a series of mix cds with DJ Shadow using all 45s. Brainfreeze, Product Placement and The Hard Sell, the last of which debuted and headlined at the world famous Hollywood Bowl. Cut’s solo album journey would begin with The Audience is Listening which was released on Warner Bros in 2006. Following his major label stint, he decided to create his own boutique label that would allow him more freedom. Sound Of The Police, Funk Off Mega Mix & his sophomore solo album, Die Cut were his most notable releases. Although these albums may sound very different from one another, they all have a single thing that ties them together - Cut Chemist pushes boundaries on all of them, testing our musical palates while introducing us to obscure musical finds.
events.title: Cut Chemist

events.summary: TICKETS ️ truewest.info/Pulp26 On Sale Friday, May 15 at 10am PT ---------------------------------------- When the members of Slow Pulp discuss Yard, their second full-length record and first for ANTI-, their vocabulary often defaults to synesthetic imagery and sensation. "We have so many visual cues for how we talk about music," singer and guitarist Emily Massey says as she stops herself in the middle of explaining how the album's second song, "Doubt," sounds like wakeboarding. "Doubt is quite dark lyrically, but it is found in this upbeat and almost campy environment." On Yard, the Wisconsin-bred, Chicago-based four-piece nestles comfortably into pockets of nuance, impressions, contradictions -- sonics and lyrics finessed together to bottle the specific tension of a feeling you've never quite been able to find the right words for. In that regard, listening to Slow Pulp can feel like being in a room with someone who's known you so long that they can read your every micro-expression and pinpoint exactly how you're feeling before you can. Perhaps this spawns from the band's own shared history and chemistry; in various ways, the four of them grew up -- are still growing up -- together. Themes of isolation and the subsequent process of learning to be comfortable with yourself sprout up throughout Yard, right alongside the importance of learning to trust, love, and lean on others. Within Slow Pulp, this trust between members is evident in the playful collaboration that remains core to Slow Pulp's creative process. Take album opener "Gone 2:" the "2" was added when they decided to scrap the first version and record a new iteration of the track just before turning the record in. They saw the video for "Scar Tissue" by the Red Hot Chili Peppers playing \(on mute\) and immediately knew the visuals were exactly what they wanted the song to sound like

events.summary: Project details: Join the Hoyt Arboretum Friends Saturday Crew to help care for the trees and trails at Hoyt Arboretum! This is a great opportunity to learn about and care for rare and unusual trees and plants from around the world. Stewardship crews occur rain or shine, so please come dressed for the weather, including long pants and sturdy, closed-toe shoes. Volunteers should bring water, snacks, and any personal items they need for the day. We provide gloves, tools, training, and parking passes. A reminder email will be sent out a week prior to the event to confirm details. Register Here Meeting location address: 4000 SW Fairview Blvd. Portland, OR 97221 Map to meeting location Parking and meeting location: Volunteers will meet in the maintenance yard behind the Hoyt Arboretum Visitor Center. There are two pay-to-park lots located near the Visitor Center, along with limited free parking along SW Fairview Blvd. Public transit: The MAX Red and Blue Lines drop off at the Washington Park Station and it's about a 15-minute walk uphill via the Overlook Trail to the meeting location. Plan your trip using the TriMet Trip Planner . Volunteers must be 16 years or older: Volunteers between 16 and 17 are welcome to volunteer without an adult, as long as a youth waiver form has been signed by an adult prior to the event. Contact Rowan for more information about this requirement. Location description and accessibility: Volunteers will be working off of established trails and on uneven surfaces. Some bending, lifting, digging, and use of various tools is required. Volunteers are encouraged to select tasks within their abilities and comfort levels. Two single-stall bathrooms and two water fountains are located at the Visitor Center, which may be up to a 15-minute walk from the work site. Questions? Contact Rowan Moreno at rowan@hoytarboretum.org rowan@hoytarboretum.org or 503-823-5453 Thank you for helping to keep Hoyt Arboretum healthy and beautiful! Here are a few tips to get you ready for your stewardship event. Stewardship Crews happen rain or shine. Please dress for the weather and wear long pants with sturdy, close-toed shoes. Bring water, snacks, and any personal items you might need. Tools, gloves, onsite training, and volunteer parking passes are provided. Registration is required for stewardship crews. Hoyt Arboretum is home to some stinging insects, and stings can occur in the park. If you have any allergies, please bring what you need to be safe and let a crew leader know ahead of time. Please stay home if you are experiencing symptoms of any contagious illness. Hoyt Arboretum welcomes groups looking to get out for a stewardship crew, however if your group is larger than five people, please reach out to schedule a private stewardship crew with us.
