events.summary: PDX CONTEMPORARY ART is pleased to present Soñé Que Revelabas, a solo exhibition of new work by photographer Georgina Reskala. The works in the exhibition center on a dream the artist had last year in which she approached her late sister, who whispered to her “Soñé que revelabas” or “I dreamed that you revealed.” Revelar in Spanish means to manifest or make public something that was secret or unknown, and is also the chemical process in photography by which a latent image becomes visible. She awoke trying to make sense of this message and wrote the sentence on a piece of paper on her studio wall. As the days and months went by, Reskala realized that she was still trying to make sense of the loss of her sister. Loss of language, interactions, moments, and memories that become fainter as a result of distance and time. This body of work became a personal account of the process of translation, not just in language, but of sounds, inflections, stories, memories, and dreams. Working with silver gelatin prints and photographs printed on textile, Reskala explores this estrangement that comes with the inability to fully translate from one language to another. Using a variety of printing techniques, she repeatedly alters her images, adding and redacting information through material processes of physically manipulating the paper, unthreading the warp and weft of the linen, and by printing, rephotographing, and reprinting the same image multiple times.
events.title: Georgina Reskala ·

events.summary: Lookout Landscape is an immersive art exhibition by Oregon-based artist and designer David Buckley Borden and a team of collaborators working across forestry, design, and engineering. Inspired by fire lookout towers, trail culture, and backcountry gear, the exhibition invites visitors onto a fabricated “Lookout Trail,” where a series of imaginative scenes—from a trailhead to a weather station, campground, and tool shed—reimagine the visual language of forestry and outdoor culture in the Pacific Northwest. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. Plan your visit and explore the exhibition: worldforestry.org/lookout-landscape

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

Filmed across nearly two decades, ADAM'S APPLE is a deeply intimate portrait of growing up, letting go, and becoming yourself. Visual artist Amy Jenkins turns the camera toward her son Adam as he moves through adolescence and into life as a trans man, while Adam brings his own writing, music and perspective to their shared story. Home movies, vérité footage and journal entries create something rare: a film about transition told from both sides of the parent-child relationship. Tender, joyful and deeply personal, ADAM'S APPLE finds its power in the rhythms of everyday adolescence: falling in love, going to prom, figuring out who you are and imagining the person you want to become. Raindrop Mandalas Tassels & Tibias S’midgins ABOUT SAMHAIN (Pronounced saw-win) Samhain is an ancient Gaelic seasonal festival, and now often celebrated by Wiccan and Pagan cultures. Modern Wicca adopted and reshaped Samhain as one of the eight Sabbats in the Wheel of the Year. Samhain is now considered a major Wiccan Sabbat celebrated from sunset on October 31 to sunset on November 1 to mark the final harvest and the beginning of the Witches' New Year. We celebrate it from October 20th through November 1st at Rae Loft.It is marked the transition from the light half of the year into the dark half. Traditionally, it was associated with the end of the harvest, the beginning of winter, and a liminal time when the boundary between the living and the dead was believed to be especially permeable.One of the best-known Samhain traditions involves large communal fires.Historical accounts describe fires being lit at important gathering places, with people and livestock participating in rituals associated with protection and purification. In later folk traditions, household fires could be extinguished and then rekindled from a communal Samhain fire.Fire symbolized protection, purification, warmth, and the continuation of life through winter.This is where modern Samhain gets much of its association with spirits and ancestors. It is called The Parting of The Veil.In traditional Gaelic belief, Samhain was considered a liminal period. Supernatural beings and the dead were thought to have greater access to the human world. People might leave food or drink for visiting spirits and ancestors. Modern Wiccans and Pagans often reinterpret this as an opportunity to: \Honor deceased loved ones \Remember ancestors \Create an ancestor altar \Light candles for those who have died and to warm the hearth and home in the coming change of season \Reflect on mortality and the cycles of life \Put up and celebrate the harvest Rae Loft is located at 2222 NE Oregon Street, Suite 207 Portland, OR 97232. No outside beverages permitted. All ages. Sorry, no dogs - we have one that works here who is healing from cancer surgery.

events.summary: This exhibition highlights a distinct artistic collaboration between printmakers Cassie Ferguson and Charlie Cohan, marking the creative intersection of their independent yet interrelated studios, Lost Bearings Press (LBP) and BurnPrint Studio (BPS). Centered on a shared dedication to traditional printmaking, the showcase features a diverse range of techniques, including stone lithography, screen printing, polyester plate lithography, and relief printmaking. The conceptual foundation of this exhibition hinges on a collaborative print created by Cohan and Ferguson in 2017, which juxtaposed the iconic Burnside Skatepark with an urban overpass. This visual conversation continues in Ferguson’s ongoing series of stone lithographs capturing DIY skateparks. Her work seeks to honor and archive the subcultural spaces that have shaped her lived experience. Because these grassroots spaces often thrive under overpasses and within neglected industrial zones, her prints seamlessly connect with Cohan’s imagery of Portland’s monumental bridges. Together, the artists offer a multifaceted view of the city, championing the gritty beauty of structural environments. Their works invite viewers to reflect on their own relationship to the municipal landscape and to find new ways of seeing everyday urban scenes. Additionally, the exhibition introduces recent work by Nakemiah “Kiki” Williams, produced in collaboration with Ferguson and Cohan at LBP and BPS. This project marks the debut publication for LBP and brings their history full circle, as both Williams and Ferguson are alumnae of Cohan’s printmaking program at the University of Hawai’i at Mānoa. This collaboration marks the beginning of collaborative print work at LBP, which is now open for publishing and contracted prints of primarily stone lithographs.
events.title: Under the Overpass

events.summary: Fat Over Lean is a free art exhibition celebrating fat bodies, fat artists, and the many ways fatness intersects with queerness, disability, identity, and belonging. Curated by Portland artist Michelle Jackson, the exhibition brings together artwork by over 30 fat artists from across the Pacific Northwest, including painting, photography, fiber, ceramics, mixed media, and more. Created in response to the lack of positive and nuanced representation of fat bodies in the arts, Fat Over Lean is about making space for people whose bodies and experiences are too often left out of galleries. The exhibition will also feature free community events and creative programming throughout October. See works by Alexis Barnes, Ana Mai Luckett, Aurora Owen, Cherie Savoie Tintary, Eko Salamanca, Fi Bu, Garrett Stache, Heather Lobitz, Heather Weitman, Jessie Wu, Jo MahnkeVanHuss, Johnny Sheckler, JUUPI, KT Kusmaul / Body Home Fat Dance, Laura Grae Miller, Lyzz Stewart, M. V. Moran, Madison Flickinger, McKinley Johnson, Michelle Jackson, Morgan Wilhelm, Nat & Jess Breece, Richelle Fullerton, Roselynn La Jeunesse, Ruby Webb, Shaun Crabb, Shayla Smith, Shelby Fercik, Miss Joomina, Sossity Chiricuzio, Stevie Rosman-Hyde, Tarina Bagua, and Uwin Hakan. Join us for these upcoming events: Opening Reception: Saturday, October 3rd, 3- 8 p.m. Why Don't I Draw Myself Fat? Saturday, October 24th from 6 - 7:30 pm. A miniature Art Show and Telltale night of storytelling and taking up space in community hosted by Telltale Presents Closing Reception/Halloween Party: Saturday, October 31st, 7 - 9 pm. About Fat Over Lean Fat Over Lean is a project that aims to lower barriers to the arts for fat, queer, and disabled people by creating opportunities to share their work within the greater Portland, Oregon, and southern Washington communities. Artists were not charged a fee to apply for this show, and they will not pay a commission on artwork sold during the exhibition, aside from standard transaction fees. We believe artists should be able to share their work without having to navigate unnecessary financial barriers. By supporting fat artists, creators, and educators, Fat Over Lean hopes to create more opportunities for growth, visibility, advancement, and connection. This project is about making room: for fat bodies, for queer and disabled voices, for artists who are often asked to take up less space, and for the communities that grow when we get to show up as ourselves. This project was made possible by RACC, Portland Arts & Culture, Fans Only Studio, and Portland Clean Air Committee. Visit Fat Over Lean or Michelle's Instagram for events and gallery hours.
events.title: Fat Over Lean Art Show & Free Events

events.summary: Q&A with Director Marc J. Francis to follow screening. “I am so grateful for the existence of this powerful and unflinching chronicle. She wanted her death to be a work of art, and so it is.” — ELIZABETH GILBERT Rayya Elias lived big. A musician, writer, hairstylist and fixture of New York’s downtown scene, she survived addiction, homelessness and incarceration before rebuilding her life on her own terms. Then, at 56, she was diagnosed with terminal cancer. By her side was her best friend turned partner, Eat, Pray, Love author Elizabeth Gilbert, who put everything else aside to care for the woman she loved. With remarkable intimacy, award-winning filmmaker Marc J. Francis follows Rayya through her final year as making music becomes more essential than ever, and she finds her way back to family, Detroit and the Arabic roots she once pushed away. Raw and deeply moving, HERE I AM is a love story, a homecoming and a portrait of an unforgettable woman determined to live fully to the end. KINDLY SPONSORED BY PIPER & ASHLEY CROWELL

events.summary: Join us as we open our doors, and close down our block, for the Altares y Muertos Opening Party. It’s a free, family-friendly afternoon celebrating Día de Muertos and the artists who bring this tradition to life across Portland’s Central Eastside. Altares y Muertos is a cultural arts program from IDEAL PDX. Since 2016, it has created spaces for remembrance, creativity, and cultural connection through community altars, workshops, artist residencies, and intergenerational learning. It has grown alongside Centro Milagro, Cargo, and neighbors throughout the Central Eastside. This fall, artists are installing ofrendas in small businesses across the neighborhood, and we’re honored to be one of them. The altars will be on display from October 24 through November 6, and this party kicks it all off. *Siempre Bailando* by Savina Monet The heart of the afternoon is Siempre Bailando, the ofrenda that local artist Savina Monet created for the distillery. We invite you to add a piece of tinsel to the altar as an offering to someone you carry with you. You can also contribute to the community ofrenda and share memories of the people you love and remember. A baile for every generation DJ Rico Ricardo, host of Portland’s Bailando Afuera dance party, is bringing the music. The baile is free and open to everyone: kids, grandparents, and everyone in between. Come dance together and connect with your ancestors across generations. Community on the street We’re closing SE Salmon in front of the distillery so local community aid organizations can set up booths. Stop by to learn about the support and resources they offer our neighbors. Food & drinks Grab tamales from La Oaxaqueña and sip specialty craft cocktails made with New Deal spirits. We’ll also have beer, wine, cider, and mocktails, so there’s something for everyone. Come celebrate life, honor memory, and dance together. We’ll see you on Salmon Street. Event Details Saturday, October 24, 2026 3–6 PM New Deal Distillery, 900 SE Salmon St, Portland, OR 97214 (corner of SE 9th & Salmon) Free and open to all ages. You must be 21+ with valid ID to purchase alcohol. Visit the ofrendas throughout the Central Eastside, October 24 – November 6

events.summary: Audience Award: Best Documentary — OUTshine LGBTQ+ Film Festival \\Jury Award: Best Documentary Film, Runner-Up — OUTshine LGBTQ+ Film Festival\*\* Audience Choice: Documentary Feature — Minneapolis St. Paul International Film Festival At 93, Roy Blakey has lived more than a few lives: theatrical figure skater, obsessive archivist and pioneering photographer of the male nude. Born in Oklahoma, Roy followed his dreams onto the ice, touring the world with Holiday on Ice before landing in New York, where his photography documented a generation of gay men and pushed the boundaries of queer image-making. Filmmaker Keri Pickett turns the camera toward her uncle and their decades-long relationship, drawing from an extraordinary personal archive of photographs, films and skating ephemera. As Roy begins to slip into dementia, preserving his remarkable legacy becomes increasingly urgent. Uncle Roy is an intimate portrait of an eccentric, fiercely private man whose extraordinary life opens a window onto a much larger queer cultural history. events.summary: Your monthly ritual... An invitation to come back to center. Our nervous systems are constantly taking in information. Between work, screens, notifications, responsibilities, and the general pace of everyday life, our attention is often being pulled in multiple directions at once—with very little intentional time to slow down and rest. This monthly nervous system reset is a dedicated space to do exactly that: support nervous system regulation. This immersive sound bath experience uses crystal singing bowls, chimes, oceanic textures, and other therapeutic sounds to gently guide your system out of the noise and stimulation of everyday life and into a deeper state of rest. For 75-minutes, there’s nowhere else you need to be and nothing you need to do. Simply get comfortable, receive the sound, and allow yourself to unwind. Think of this as your recurring monthly ritual to come back to center - a space to intentionally step away from the busyness of life, reconnect with yourself, and give your body and mind the restoration you're craving. Come as you are. Yoga mats, blankets, and props are available for your use, but please feel free to bring anything that will help you feel even more cozy & comfortable. These sessions are open to all; no prior experience is needed. About Kristi Kristi Littman is a certified sound healing practitioner & facilitation teacher whose heart-led approach blends nervous system awareness, intuition, and deep presence. Since 2019, Kristi has held space for thousands of people through community sound baths, corporate wellness, sound healing training, and 1:1 mentorship. She blends crystal singing bowls, chimes, and oceanic tones to create immersive soundscapes designed to soothe the nervous system and realign the body’s natural rhythms. She often weaves in meditation and breathwork, offering grounded, intuitive guidance that helps participants soften, release, and remember their own inner wisdom. A two-time World Cup champion, Olympic gold medalist, proud queer icon and former University of Portland Pilot, she transformed women’s soccer while becoming one of the most fearless voices of her generation. events.summary: Glen Canyon Institute, in collaboration with the Deschutes River Alliance and WaterWatch of Oregon, presents What the River Knows, a Glen Canyon documentary by Good Intentions Paving Co. Today, a lost Eden emerges from beneath Lake Powell, revealing both the consequences of past mistakes and the potential for a new path forward for the Colorado River. What The River Knows explores this pivotal moment, where the urgent need to rethink water management in the West aligns with an opportunity to restore a stunning landscape and flooded ancestral homeland. Amidst the grim discussions surrounding climate change and the Colorado River crisis, the film tells a powerful story of nature’s resilience: Glen Canyon is coming back to life. The evening will open with a documentary short from the Deschutes River Alliance. The Last 100 Miles: The Fight for the lower Deschutes River portrays the degradation of one of the finest trout and salmon sanctuaries anywhere in the world, and the work by those who love the river to save it. Following the film screening, the event will conclude with a panel discussion and audience Q+A.
events.title: What the River Knows, a Colorado River Documentary

As if that weren’t enough, the destruction has brought another threat out of the shadows: zombies. This year’s interactive, no-contact haunted theatre drops you into the middle of the invasion. Choose how you face the apocalypse: Join the Resistance Rent an optional laser-tag weapon \(\+$2\) and fight back. The equipment uses a safe, invisible infrared beam to activate designated targets and trigger special effects as you move through the theatre. Become a Refugee Prefer not to use laser tag? Make your way through the ruined city as a refugee, trying to escape with your life while danger waits around every corner. Apocalypse in the Grove may include fog, laser lighting, loud noises, strobe effects, simulated fire, cold sparks, sudden scares, and intense theatrical environments. Will you join the resistance—or simply try to survive? When you purchase a ticket, you purchase a reservation for a 30 minute window. You must arrive in this timeframe or your entry could be delayed or denied. There are 6 people in each tour of the haunted theatre. This experience is wheelchair accessible. Anthropology is about a grieving computer coder, Merril, who builds an AI replica of her missing and presumed dead sister. events.summary: Our audiences have been asking us to bring back the Halloween show for years…. Be careful what you wish for. Stephen Mallatratt’s The Woman in Black has been terrifying audiences since its London debut in 1987 and is one of the most successful and terrifying shows in West End history. Based on Susan Hill’s beloved novel, it’s one of the most celebrated ghost stories ever staged: atmospheric, relentless, and the kind of theatrical experience that makes you question every shadow on your way to the car. Set in a remote English village, it follows a young lawyer unraveling the secrets of a recently deceased client and the vengeful presence that doesn’t want him to. Just two actors portray all the characters, leaning into what B&B’s performers do best. Chilling, clever, and unforgettable. Halloween is back at Bag&Baggage…and we brought something with us. events.summary: "Marigolds y Memorias" is an original devised production inspired by the traveling carpa tradition, in which humor, music, and storytelling come together in a vibrant theatrical journey. Guided by an elder, a younger generation learns to build an altar, the heart of Día de Muertos, discovering the meaning behind each of its elements, from candles and marigolds to photographs, ofrendas, and cherished recuerdos. Through song, dance, and short theatrical vignettes, the altar gradually takes shape as an act of remembrance and cultural inheritance, inviting audiences to consider how traditions are taught, how memory is kept alive, and what is carried forward when we share rituals across generations. events.summary: Portland favorites Tree Frogs bring their eclectic blend of roots rock, improvisation, and groove-driven songwriting to Tomorrow's Verse for an evening of music shaped by decades of playing together. Drawing from rock, country, folk, blues, funk, and soul, the band has built a reputation for shows that feel both relaxed and adventurous, where strong songs provide the foundation for unexpected musical turns. A fixture of the Pacific Northwest music scene since the early 1990s, Tree Frogs spent much of that decade on the road, playing more than 500 shows across the U.S. and Europe in support of three releases: Tree Frogs Live! (1994), Leap Year (1996), and Live at the Laurelthirst (1997). After taking a break from touring, the band returned in 2000 and has remained a steady presence at clubs, festivals, and neighborhood venues throughout the region ever since. What sets Tree Frogs apart isn't virtuosity or spectacle, but chemistry. Years of shared stages have given the band a natural musical connection that allows songs to stretch, breathe, and evolve in the moment. One tune might lean into a deep country groove, while the next finds its way toward funk, blues, or classic rock territory. Whether you're a longtime fan or catching them for the first time, expect an evening of road-tested musicianship, thoughtful songwriting, and the kind of warm, communal atmosphere that has kept Northwest audiences coming back for years.
events.title: Tree Frogs

events.summary: Will these stories stay behind glass, or will you open a door to the past? Something isn't right here. That book is out of place. There is a card in the display case, but no item behind it. There are antiques in the incorrect place; and artefacts that are standing wrong side up. Clearly, the venue needs your help. As curators of other nearby museums, you are called to the venue after hours in order to help figure out what is causing these disturbances. Once inside, you are greeted by one of the exhibits who has come to life. They are happy to show you around and share tales about the other exhibits. As you hear stories from their lives, it becomes clear that one of them is the culprit behind these disturbances. The question is, which one? Succeed and you will find yourself promoted. Fail, and you may find yourself trapped behind glass forever. Enter an immersive historic experience where exhibits come to life, and there’s a mystery for you to solve! Presented by Live History, a Governor General’s Award nominated international touring theatre company who produces site specific customizable mysteries around the world, and the Oswego Heritage Council.
events.title: Behind Glass Escape Room

events.summary: 34 Years Later: A Seattle Pearl Jam Celebration Washed in Black is stoked to be back at Billy Blues Bar & Grill for a very special night celebrating Pearl Jam, Seattle music history, and the community that has kept this music alive for more than three decades. October 1990 marked the very beginning of Pearl Jam as a live band in Seattle — from their first show at the Off Ramp to the early rehearsal and demo sessions that helped launch one of the most important bands of the era. 34 years later, we’re celebrating those Seattle roots — just south in Vancouver. Washed in Black will take the stage for an epic live Pearl Jam experience, digging beyond the hits and deep into the catalog with rarities, deep cuts, fan favorites, and songs you don’t hear every night. If you miss the days when flannel was king and the Seattle sound was changing rock music forever, this one is for you. SPECIAL GUEST: NICK MARDON TRIO We’re fired up to have our very own Nick Mardon bringing the Nick Mardon Trio out to kick off the night. The Seattle-based blues-rock power trio features Nick Mardon on guitar and vocals, Adin Pennington on bass and vocals, and Andy Emery on drums. Their sound blends the raw power of ’60s and ’70s blues-rock with the Seattle sound of the 1990s. After hundreds of shows throughout the Pacific Northwest, they’ve built a massive repertoire featuring original music along with timeless covers from artists including Jimi Hendrix, Stevie Ray Vaughan, Led Zeppelin, Pearl Jam, Sublime, Lynyrd Skynyrd, Eric Clapton, Johnny Cash and more. Come early. Catch Nick Mardon Trio. Stay for the definitive Pearl Jam tribute experience. SATURDAY, OCTOBER 24 Billy Blues Bar & Grill 7115 NE Hazel Dell Ave Vancouver, WA Doors: 7 PM Show: 8 PM $15 at the door 21\+ WASHED IN BLACK — A TRIBUTE TO PEARL JAM NICK MARDON TRIO — Originals & Timeless Covers BACK IN THE PORTLAND / VANCOUVER SCENE. Relive some memories. Make some new ones. Make America Grunge Again. Salud!

events.summary: Daði Freyr is an Icelandic singer, songwriter, and producer known for his witty lyricism, infectious synth-pop, and joyful unpredictability. He rose to global attention with his 2020 hit "Think About Things", which went viral during lockdown, earning over 100 million streams and praise from P!nk, James Corden, and Russell Crowe. His new album Too Much, Not Enough, out May 8th, marks a new chapter. Co-written with collaborators for the first time, it's his most emotionally honest work yet: a record about self-acceptance, about being who you actually are rather than who you think others want to see. After years in Berlin, Daði returned to Iceland in 2025, and that sense of coming home, of settling into something real, runs through every track. This autumn, Daði brings his live show to the US and Canada. Performing alone on stage with self-built instruments and hand-crafted visuals, it's an intimate, one-of-a-kind experience and the connection with his audience remains, as ever, the thing he loves most.

events.summary: In a backyard studio she calls the “Temple of Bloom,” Laura Veirs made a record without a safety net. No click. No headphones. No edits. Temple Songs is her first fully self-recorded and self-produced album—a collection of performances captured live, where feeling takes precedence over polish. The songs unfold with a raw, luminous quality, tracing arcs of devotion, independence, and creative renewal. Out August 14, 2026. FULL BIO: Singer-songwriter Laura Veirs has produced 15 albums over 28 years, has toured internationally and has collaborated with luminaries such as kd lang, Neko Case, Sufjan Stevens, Jim James \(of My Morning Jacket\), The Decemberists, Bill Frisell and many more. Her music blends the poetic sensibilities of contemporary folk with the melodic frameworks of indie rock. Veirs’ songs are literate and emotionally intelligent. Her work has been praised in the New York Times, The Guardian, The Independent, The Washington Post and many other publications. She also is a published author, podcaster, teacher and painter. She lives in Portland, OR with her blended family of 4 teens, a husband, a dog and a cat.

events.summary: From behind the redwood curtain of Humboldt County, California, the seven piece funk-soul band Diggin Dirt has carved out a niche as a live party not to be missed. Shoveling their own path, Diggin Dirt has seen sustained growth over the past few years, with multiple national tours and festival stops at Jam Cruise, High Sierra, Hulaween, Same Same but Different, Live Oak, Cascade Equinox, Joshua Tree Music Festival and many more. Per a 2024 Jam Cruise writer, “This was the soul music I grew up with in the ‘60s and ‘70s, but I confess I wasn’t expecting \[Diggin Dirt\] to be throwing it down this hard. This group is impossibly tight, and Zach Alder might be the best soul shouter I’ve ever heard, and I’ve heard a few.” Their infectious sound is fueled by blazing horns, searing guitars and a relentlessly driving rhythm section, and tying it all together is the band’s frontman who launches the ensemble into rarefied air with his pipes, charisma and natural-born soul. With flashes of James Brown or Sly and the Family Stone, Otis Redding or Tower of Power, the band’s sound is both familiar and yet refreshingly original, layering psychedelic rock, Motown soul, afrobeat and even reggae atop a thick foundation of late-60s inspired funk.

events.summary: Director and QDoc alum, Jeffrey Schwarz in attendance. WORLD PREMIERE — TRIBECA FESTIVAL 2026 “Captures a poignant tipping point in pre-AIDS queer culture.” — Guy Lodge, Variety In 1979, William Friedkin descended on New York’s West Village to make Cruising, his controversial thriller starring Al Pacino as a cop hunting a serial killer in the city’s gay leather bars. The production ignited fierce protests from queer activists who feared the film would turn gay men into predators and victims at a moment when the community was fighting for visibility and dignity. But behind the Hollywood controversy was a real-life tragedy. Jeffrey Schwarz (VITO, TAB HUNTER CONFIDENTIAL) traces the story of Addison Verrill, a young Variety reporter murdered in 1977 after a night at the Mineshaft, while revisiting the vanished world of pre-AIDS New York that surrounded him. Part true crime, part queer cultural history, Mineshaft asks what gets remembered when Hollywood turns real lives into fiction. KINDLY SPONSORED BY HOWIE BIERBAUM, TOM BARRETO & BRIAN SINCLAIR.
events.title: MINESHAFT: THE CRUISING MURDERS

events.summary: Grammy nominated producer and songwriter Audien has established himself as a fixture in the dance community, known for his production prowess and unique propensity for uplifting melodies. Considered a staple in the progressive house genre, Audien launched his career in 2008 with a string of releases on Anjunabeats, Armada Music, Spinnin’ Records, and Astralwerks. Over the years Audien solidified his signature sound and garnered the support of industry veterans like Tiësto, Above & Beyond, and Armin van Buuren. In 2014, Audien released his Grammy nominated remix of Bastille’s “Pompeii”, which went on to become the most played track at Electric Daisy Carnival and Coachella, and one of the five most played tracks at Tomorrowland. It is no surprise then that Audien has become a mainstay at marquee festival brands across the world including Tomorrowland, EDC, Ultra, Lollapalooza, and many more. Audien’s career growth and influence is evidenced by his impressive list of collaborators, which include Lady Antebellum, MAX, and Echosmith, on top of official remixes for Michael Jackson, Coldplay, and Halsey. Audien released his debut LP ‘Escapism’ in November 2019. The album is a definitive effort encapsulating both Audien’s signature style and his dominance in the dance landscape. Audien states, “I’m not reinventing the wheel, but I’m accentuating the art I’ve created for almost a decade. It’s the best form of what I’m known for.”
events.title: Audien

Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Q&A with QDoc alums Director Jennifer Kroot and Editor Bill Weber, joined by Sister Roma, Sister Lida, and Honey Mahogany to follow the screening. “In a time of uncertainty and anguish, HUNKY JESUS is balm for the soul.” — Gavin Spoors, FILMHOUNDS Every Easter Sunday in San Francisco, the Sisters of Perpetual Indulgence turn celebration into an act of resistance. Director, Jennifer M. Kroot (THE UNTOLD TALES OF ARMISTEAD MAUPIN, TO BE TAKEI) dives into the annual tradition where drag, burlesque, religious parody and outrageous pageantry collide in an expression of queer community and radical joy. Anchored in the 2023 celebration, the film blends performances, candid interviews and rare archival footage to trace four decades of the Sisters’ fearless activism, from confronting the Catholic Church to advocating for those pushed to the margins. With Sister Roma, RUPAUL’S DRAG RACE alum Honey Mahogany, and voiceover by George Takei, HUNKY JESUS is funny, irreverent and unexpectedly moving, celebrating a community that has made an art form of challenging hypocrisy while welcoming everyone to the party. Raindrop Mandalas Tassels & Tibias S’midgins ABOUT SAMHAIN (Pronounced saw-win) Samhain is an ancient Gaelic seasonal festival, and now often celebrated by Wiccan and Pagan cultures. Modern Wicca adopted and reshaped Samhain as one of the eight Sabbats in the Wheel of the Year. Samhain is now considered a major Wiccan Sabbat celebrated from sunset on October 31 to sunset on November 1 to mark the final harvest and the beginning of the Witches' New Year. We celebrate it from October 20th through November 1st at Rae Loft.It is marked the transition from the light half of the year into the dark half. Traditionally, it was associated with the end of the harvest, the beginning of winter, and a liminal time when the boundary between the living and the dead was believed to be especially permeable.One of the best-known Samhain traditions involves large communal fires.Historical accounts describe fires being lit at important gathering places, with people and livestock participating in rituals associated with protection and purification. In later folk traditions, household fires could be extinguished and then rekindled from a communal Samhain fire.Fire symbolized protection, purification, warmth, and the continuation of life through winter.This is where modern Samhain gets much of its association with spirits and ancestors. It is called The Parting of The Veil.In traditional Gaelic belief, Samhain was considered a liminal period. Supernatural beings and the dead were thought to have greater access to the human world. People might leave food or drink for visiting spirits and ancestors. Modern Wiccans and Pagans often reinterpret this as an opportunity to: \Honor deceased loved ones \Remember ancestors \Create an ancestor altar \Light candles for those who have died and to warm the hearth and home in the coming change of season \Reflect on mortality and the cycles of life \Put up and celebrate the harvest Rae Loft is located at 2222 NE Oregon Street, Suite 207 Portland, OR 97232. No outside beverages permitted. All ages. Sorry, no dogs - we have one that works here who is healing from cancer surgery.
events.title: Wicked Craft: Samhain Mystical Market

events.summary: Fat Over Lean is a free art exhibition celebrating fat bodies, fat artists, and the many ways fatness intersects with queerness, disability, identity, and belonging. Curated by Portland artist Michelle Jackson, the exhibition brings together artwork by over 30 fat artists from across the Pacific Northwest, including painting, photography, fiber, ceramics, mixed media, and more. Created in response to the lack of positive and nuanced representation of fat bodies in the arts, Fat Over Lean is about making space for people whose bodies and experiences are too often left out of galleries. The exhibition will also feature free community events and creative programming throughout October. See works by Alexis Barnes, Ana Mai Luckett, Aurora Owen, Cherie Savoie Tintary, Eko Salamanca, Fi Bu, Garrett Stache, Heather Lobitz, Heather Weitman, Jessie Wu, Jo MahnkeVanHuss, Johnny Sheckler, JUUPI, KT Kusmaul / Body Home Fat Dance, Laura Grae Miller, Lyzz Stewart, M. V. Moran, Madison Flickinger, McKinley Johnson, Michelle Jackson, Morgan Wilhelm, Nat & Jess Breece, Richelle Fullerton, Roselynn La Jeunesse, Ruby Webb, Shaun Crabb, Shayla Smith, Shelby Fercik, Miss Joomina, Sossity Chiricuzio, Stevie Rosman-Hyde, Tarina Bagua, and Uwin Hakan. Join us for these upcoming events: Opening Reception: Saturday, October 3rd, 3- 8 p.m. Why Don't I Draw Myself Fat? Saturday, October 24th from 6 - 7:30 pm. A miniature Art Show and Telltale night of storytelling and taking up space in community hosted by Telltale Presents Closing Reception/Halloween Party: Saturday, October 31st, 7 - 9 pm. About Fat Over Lean Fat Over Lean is a project that aims to lower barriers to the arts for fat, queer, and disabled people by creating opportunities to share their work within the greater Portland, Oregon, and southern Washington communities. Artists were not charged a fee to apply for this show, and they will not pay a commission on artwork sold during the exhibition, aside from standard transaction fees. We believe artists should be able to share their work without having to navigate unnecessary financial barriers. By supporting fat artists, creators, and educators, Fat Over Lean hopes to create more opportunities for growth, visibility, advancement, and connection. This project is about making room: for fat bodies, for queer and disabled voices, for artists who are often asked to take up less space, and for the communities that grow when we get to show up as ourselves. This project was made possible by RACC, Portland Arts & Culture, Fans Only Studio, and Portland Clean Air Committee. Visit Fat Over Lean or Michelle's Instagram for events and gallery hours.

events.summary: We Built You a Garden is the third installment of Metro’s Community Voices project, a multimedia storytelling initiative that invites residents of Metro Affordable Housing Bond-funded communities to explore the meaning of home through photography, writing and collective reflection. Hosted through a summer workshop series at the Strong Empowerment Village in partnership with artists Gwen Hoeffgen and Domenic Toliver, the project centers the experiences of residents with ties to North and Northeast Portland. Through weekly workshops and the use of film photography and creative writing, participants documented places, people and memories that shape their understanding of home, legacy and belonging. Their work considers displacement, resilience and community history, creating a powerful collection of stories that honor the past while imagining what can continue to grow. Ultimately, We Built You a Garden asks what’s been inherited, what’s been built, and what we want to leave growing for the next generation. It speaks to the ongoing impact of displacement in Portland for the Black community, but it also affirms what it took — and continues to take — to nourish, tend and build home. Exhibition and events: Free admission Oct. 9, 5:30pm to 8pm: We Built You a Garden | Exhibition Opening at The BLACK Gallery Join us for the opening of We Built You a Garden, with remarks and refreshments as well as free copies of the project’s publication. Open to public with remarks from Metro, artists, and Don’t Shoot PDX . Oct. 23, 6pm to 8pm: We Built You a Garden | Community Conversation at The BLACK Gallery A conversation about the past, present, and future of Portland through the experiences of the people who live, work, organize, and build here. Artists, activists, community members, youth and Metro come together to consider what we have inherited, what we have built, what is changing, and what we want to leave growing for the next generation. The BLACK Gallery will be open to the public on the following Sundays from 1pm to 4pm during the exhibition’s display: Oct. 11, Oct. 18, Oct. 25 and Nov. 1.
events.title: We Built You a Garden

Nick Lucifer in Club Hell, performed by Sean Lujan (Design for Living, Salomé) and Blavatsky, performed by Anne Sorce (Nice People, Happyness). NICK LUCIFER IN CLUB HELL The story of the universe told by a weathered gangster in “Club Hell” located well down below. BLAVATSKY Madame Blavatsky welcomes you to her private inner quarters to witness truth, lies, psychic phenomena, chickens, monkeys, nonsense, foolishness and drivel. “I’ve always wondered how many great artists have never been recognized. I would venture many. “I believe Don Nigro was a genius of theatre you never heard of” says director Jerry Mouawad. After I selected four of his works earlier this year, Nigro died. The Flying Solo Festival, which features four of his solos, has now become a homage to Nigro’s prolific work - he wrote over 500 plays!” American Theatre’s Lawrence Harbison wrote “he was hardly on the radar. Why not? Don lived in a small house in Northeast Ohio with his father, a disabled veteran who had been seriously wounded in the Battle of the Bulge and needed constant care. So, Don couldn’t travel, making it hard for him to do the sort of networking so important for establishing a reputation. And, anyway, he would rather stay home and write.” Production Credits: *Light Design:* Ronnie Rantis Costume Design: Laura Helgeson Sound Design: Myrrh Larsen Note: For Mature Audiences

Stephen Mallatratt’s The Woman in Black has been terrifying audiences since its London debut in 1987 and is one of the most successful and terrifying shows in West End history. Based on Susan Hill’s beloved novel, it’s one of the most celebrated ghost stories ever staged: atmospheric, relentless, and the kind of theatrical experience that makes you question every shadow on your way to the car. events.summary: "Marigolds y Memorias" is an original devised production inspired by the traveling carpa tradition, in which humor, music, and storytelling come together in a vibrant theatrical journey. Guided by an elder, a younger generation learns to build an altar, the heart of Día de Muertos, discovering the meaning behind each of its elements, from candles and marigolds to photographs, ofrendas, and cherished recuerdos. Through song, dance, and short theatrical vignettes, the altar gradually takes shape as an act of remembrance and cultural inheritance, inviting audiences to consider how traditions are taught, how memory is kept alive, and what is carried forward when we share rituals across generations. Age Recommendation: All Ages Estimated Running Time: 1 hour 30 minutes, including one intermission

events.summary: End your weekend slowly with sound, sauna, and rest. Join us at Koti, a neighborhood Finnish sauna tucked into a quiet residential neighborhood in Milwaukie, for a Sunday evening of sound, warmth, and time to unwind. We'll begin with an immersive 60-minute sound bath led by Kristi Littman. Through the resonant sounds of crystal singing bowls, you'll have an opportunity to settle in, quiet your mind, and enjoy an hour of uninterrupted rest. Afterward, we'll head outside for two unhurried hours of traditional Finnish sauna, cold plunging, and time around the fire. In Finland, sauna is an ordinary and cherished part of everyday life. It's a place to slow down, connect with others, and enjoy the simple pleasure of getting warm. At Koti, we've brought that tradition into our own backyard, with a cedar sauna, the gentle steam of löyly, fresh-water cold plunges, and space to enjoy the outdoors. There's no prescribed routine or pace to follow. Enjoy the heat, cool off when you're ready, sit by the fire, and settle into the evening however feels good to you. What to bring: Please bring a yoga mat for the sound bath. You're also welcome to bring a blanket, pillow, warm socks, or anything else that makes you extra comfortable. Bring your swimsuit and two towels (one small one for sitting on in the sauna and one for drying off). All are welcome. No prior sound bath or sauna experience is needed.
events.title: Sunday Slowdown: Sound Bath + Sauna

events.summary: Q&A with Director Cheri Gaulke and Writer/Producer Anne Gauldin to follow screening. Swift House Prize for Best Depiction of the Arts — Middlebury New Filmmakers Festival, 2026. “Gaulke’s argument is that this was not a fringe but a foundation.” — Martin Cid Magazine. In 1970s Los Angeles, a radical community of women artists picked up cameras, took to the streets and turned their own bodies into art, activism and rebellion. At the center was the Woman’s Building, a groundbreaking feminist art space where performance became a tool for exploring gender, sexuality and identity, while challenging who got to make art in the first place. Filmmaker and pioneering performance artist Cheri Gaulke returns to the movement that shaped her, weaving her own journey from minister’s daughter to lesbian artist and activist into a remarkable archive of rarely seen performances and the voices of the women who created them. Executive produced by Lily Tomlin and Jane Wagner, Acting Like Women is a spirited reclamation of a revolutionary chapter of queer and feminist art history. Featuring music by Billie Eilish, The Linda Lindas, Fanny, Phranc and Holly Near. KINDLY SPONSORED BY LISA SCHIMMEL & MADISON WEISS, SNOWMADE AND PAUL CHEEK. SUPPORTING SPONSOR & COMMUNITY PARTNER: LESBIAN CULTURE CLUB
events.title: ACTING LIKE WOMEN

events.summary: See the award-winning short documentary featuring a beloved Portland icon, then join a post-screening walking tour to view the Thompson Elk and other monuments that shape the story of our city. At the Portland Art Museum. Film begins at 4:00pm. Tour Begins at 5:00pm. Event is part of the ADX Festival. About the Film: The Elk - 30 min Documentary As protest consumed Portland, Ore. in 2020, the city removed a beloved elk sculpture for safekeeping. Six years later, the elk is the first of the city's damaged monuments to return, and the only sculpture without controversy. But in a city that never really stopped protesting, people remain divided over why the elk went away—and what it means for the dinged-up but refurbished symbol to finally return. Set in an American city reckoning with its symbols of westward expansion, the unfolding fate of the elk and the other sculptures tells the story of a nation divided over who and what belongs on a pedestal. About the Walking Tour: Tour guide Sarah Gilbert of Around Portland Tours is a featured participant in the film, The Elk. Sarah is a writer and bicycle evangelist, and has worked in the hiking tourism industry for over a decade. Join Sarah and Director Erika Bolstad on a localized tour of downtown Portland monuments, including the Thompson Elk. The tour is free and starts immediately after the screening and Q&A for The Elk, outside the Portland Art Museum.
events.title: The Elk - Film Screening and Walking Tour

events.summary: Sundays 4:30PM - 5:30PM, Oct 4 - Dec 20 | $10/weekly drop in Need a reset for your busy week ahead? Join us Sunday late afternoons for a welcoming, beginner-friendly yoga class focused on foundational poses, mindful movement, breath awareness, and building confidence on the mat. Whether you’re brand new to yoga or looking to reconnect with the fundamentals, this class is designed to help you build a strong foundation through accessible movement, breath work, and foundational poses. We’ll focus on alignment, balance, flexibility, and body awareness in a welcoming, supportive environment. Beginners are encouraged to join, and those with a regular practice will also benefit from slowing down, refining technique, and deepening their understanding of familiar poses. Options and modifications will be offered throughout class so everyone can move at their own pace. Wear comfortable athletic clothes, bring a yoga mat if possible \(a limited number will be available to borrow\), and please arrive 5–10 minutes before class begins so we can start on time. Classes are led by Wyle O'Neill, from Love Our Practice, whose yoga journey began in high school and later led him to study in Mysore and Goa, India, where he deepened his understanding of yoga’s roots and philosophy. Wyle completed his 200-hour RYT training at Yoga Salt with Tamal Dodge and completed his 500-hour teacher training at Sthira Yoga School in Goa, India. His teaching blends accessible movement, meditation, breathwork through an individual-centered practice to help students feel grounded, present, as well as connected to themselves and community.

events.summary: At a time when many theatres are closing their doors or reducing programming, 100 Lives Repertory in Portland’s Buckman neighborhood is celebrating the inaugural season in its brand-new space. And the first play is a doozy: a sleek, sly, sci-fi mystery titled Anthropology, penned by Lauren Gunderson, one of America’s most produced playwrights. Anthropology is about a grieving computer coder, Merril, who builds an AI replica of her missing and presumed dead sister. Adding to the loss, Merril’s relationship with her girlfriend has come to an end, which draws her deeper and deeper into her ‘project’ of bringing back a version of her sister, to help heal her grief and lessen her loneliness. This is the Oregon premiere of Anthropology which had its world debut in London at Hampstead Theatre in 2023. The play runs Thursday through Sunday from October 23 through November 15. It features an all-female, four-actor cast and is directed by 100 Lives Rep’s Executive Director Cat Plein. Due to nudity and sexual situations, it is recommended only for adult audiences.

events.summary: Glass. Kill. Bluebeard. Imp. is a collection of four short, surreal plays by acclaimed English playwright, Caryl Churchill. Premiering at London's Royal Court Theatre in 2019, these darkly imaginative works weave together myth, fairy tale, and contemporary horror. Moving between collective voices and intimate encounters, Churchill explores violence, power, desire, and the stories we tell to make sense of a fractured world. By turns funny, haunting, and unsettling, the plays invite audiences into a landscape where the familiar becomes strange and ancient myths reveal modern anxieties without explanation or comfort. A girl made of glass. Gods and murders. A serial killer's friends. And a secret in a bottle.​ Four short plays by Caryl Churchill Directed by Samantha Van Der Merwe​October 10th - November 7th 2026
events.title: Glass. Kill. Bluebeard. Imp. by Caryl Churchill

events.summary: Q&A with Carole Pope and Director Michelle Mama to follow the screening. Best Canadian Feature — Inside Out 2SLGBTQ+ Film Festival Audience Award: Best in Show — Queer North Film Festival Audience Award: Best Documentary — Queer North Film Festival Three-time Juno Award-winning queer rock icon Carole Pope was singing openly about lesbian desire on daytime radio before the culture had any idea what to do with her. As frontwoman of Rough Trade, Pope tore through 1970s and ’80s Toronto with sexually charged lyrics, punk-glam swagger and a refusal to make herself more palatable. Decades later, she’s still writing, performing and pushing back. Director Michelle Mama (SUMMER QAMP) follows Pope as she reckons with aging, love, loss and an industry that never quite knew where to put her. With electrifying archival footage and interviews with k.d. lang, Peaches, Jann Arden and Rufus Wainwright, ANTIDIVA is funny, sexy and defiantly alive. CLOSING NIGHT IS KINDLY SPONSORED BY TY SMART AND JESSY BAROS FRIEDT COMMUNITY PARTNER: MENOPUNKS

The hotel's supernatural allure inhabits its guests (and staff) in this dilapidated relic of the past. The Hitchcocks' latest hire is no exception. The graveyard "maitre d," quickly realizes that there has been a misunderstanding in the hiring process and that he's been mistakenly hired for the precarious “night shift” position, one unfit for pedigree. He is about to experience nothing short of a fortuitous paranormal entanglement unlike any other. events.summary: Some words from other folks on the new record “below your knows” No dog ever eats Luke Callen’s homework. He does it all. He turns it in ahead of time. Not for a grade. Not for extra credit. It’s his work and he’s good at it. Poet. Singer. Player. Just listen. First he captures your attention. You want to make comparisons with the giants whose shoulders he stood on. But don’t. He’s plenty tall enough in his own bare feet and his shoulders are wide enough to hold up the next batch of poets, singers, players. Keep listening. Now he captures your imagination. Luke is the hitch-hiker who picks you up. Get in. Toss your bindle in the back. Have you got a couple bucks for gas? No matter. He’s going take you all around the world. Pay attention. He’s going to show you everything that’s in it. And it’s right Below Your Knows. -Eddie Allen Below your knows gets better with every listen. The album has a great atmosphere, it is one of those rarities that once you start it, you have to listen to the end. It is a standout, I get the same feeling from this album as I get from listening to albums like Dead Kennedy’s – Bedtime for Democracy, or Grateful Dead – Live/Dead, or Al Scorch – Circle Round the Signs. Below your knows takes you on a sonic journey and hits the listener in their soul. It is amazing, the music connects you with a “life force”…to others, the Earth, and the stars. The songs are something special; they feel so genuine and heartfelt. It’s truly rare to find music like this out there these days. The songs take one on an introspective journey and forces you to answer the question “Are you fucking alive?!”. By the time the album finishes, you are left with the question….what next? Hit Fucking Play. – Eric Peloza Take heed, take heed, Luke Callen has a great new song “a walk out of doors” from his upcoming album, Below Your Knows. An album built out of the roots that once was American folk music. It’s simple, earthy, and raw. “A walk out of doors” is the first track off the album and it is nothing short of a masterpiece. It’s beautiful and gritty. I don’t know if it’s the tonal quality of the resonator, or Callen’s vocals, but I could listen to this song ten thousand times and never grow tired. The lyrics paint a beautiful picture, the resonator places you within the picture, and Callen’s voice makes it so you never want to leave. I feel like I’m sitting down around a campfire listening to Callen as if he’s right there in front of me. It’s incredibly intimate and I want nothing more than to witness him performing the song live. – lttlbrthr Luke Callen is originally from the river town of La Crosse, WI-the heart of the Driftless Region-and currently lives in Minneapolis, MN by way of Colorado. A teller of tall tales and a singer of short tunes-Luke lugs around a couple of guitars-a few harmonicas and even a banjo if he has to. A simple writer and liver who cares more about his cast irons than he does about his interweb streams-Luke is now on tour and will be for the foreseeable future. To track him down and see a live show for yourself…please just get in touch. Having steeped himself-like a cheap bag of tea that you found in a drawer you rarely open-in the recording’s of Harry Smith’s Anthology of American Folk Music, to campfires, classrooms, honky tonks, festivals and clubs across the country, Luke brings his humble sense of humor and humanity. With his Chevy Astro greased up, Luke has played hundreds of shows spanning both coasts, the American west, south and heartland. He has had the opportunity to provide support for Dom Flemons, Dead Horses, The Dustbowl Revival, Kacy & Clayton, James McMurtry, Whiskey Shivers, Charlie Parr, The Lowest Pair, The Last Revel, Lilly Hiatt, Chicago Farmer, and Robbie Fulks among others.
events.title: Luke Callen & Bad Posture Club

events.summary: Join us for a special FREE SHOW with Dusk Dept. and special guest Greaterkind \+ A Very Good DJ Set from Alex Wasily! No names, no faces, just grooves. Dusk Dept. is a seven-piece collective emerging from the deep corners of the modern funk underground…a shadowy convergence of musicians whose fingerprints can be found on the grooves of the heaviest hitters in the lineage of rhythm. Formed unofficially from the raging of late night sessions that transformed into full-fledged studio recordings, Dusk Dept. keeps its members hidden beneath black hoods, trading ego & resumes for atmosphere, and identity for collective creating. Onstage, the robes blur every boundary…between player and audience, between band and ritual, between now and the memory of some older recording that felt cutting edge that you just discovered that you now can’t remember. Their debut, a self-titled album on Ear Up Records (founded by Jeff Coffin of the Dave Matthews Band), sounds like the meeting point of the sacred and the filthy; analog funk baptized in mystery. Seven players. Seven voices. One department in charge of the night shift. Dusk Dept. doesn’t announce itself. It appears… an injection of brass, a thump of bass, a silhouette under dim lights. Then it’s gone, leaving behind only sweat, grooves, and questions.

events.summary: TICKETS ️ truewest.info/DEP26 On Sale Friday, June 19 at 10am PT ---------------------------------------- w/ XCOMM & Squid Pisser The Dillinger Escape Plan Born out of the late-’90s New Jersey hardcore underground, The Dillinger Escape Plan detonated onto the extreme music scene with a sound that felt less like a band and more like a structural collapse in real time. With the release of their landmark 1999 debut album Calculating Infinity, the group redefined the boundaries of hardcore, metal, and experimental music through impossible time signatures, violent precision, and a chaotic live presence that quickly became legendary. The Dillinger Escape Plan fused mathcore complexity with grindcore intensity and punk unpredictability. Tracks like “43% Burnt,” “Sugar Coated Sour,” and “Destro’s Secret” sounded mechanical yet deeply human — controlled explosions stitched together with razor-sharp musicianship. At a time when heavy music was becoming increasingly polished and formulaic, The Dillinger Escape Plan embraced dissonance, instability, and outright danger. The Calculating Infinity era became synonymous with total sensory overload. Their live shows were infamous for shattered equipment, stage-dives from impossible heights, and performances that blurred the line between catharsis and collapse. Yet beneath the chaos was a level of compositional sophistication that would influence an entire generation of progressive metal, hardcore, and experimental bands for decades to come. More than just a debut record, Calculating Infinity remains a defining statement in heavy music — an album that challenged listeners, alienated purists, and established The Dillinger Escape Plan as one of the most fearless and innovative acts of their era. XCOMM are a Venice Beach hardcore punk band making fast, furious, sharply self-aware music with the rare combination of youthful volatility, serious songwriting chops and absolutely no interest in waiting their turn. Formed in 2023, XCOMM are frontman Michael Gatto, bassist Adan Escoto, guitarist Eric Matt, DJ Hunter Grogan and drummer Revel Ian. Their debut album, Time To Burn, is out now via Blowed Out Records, the label and incubator founded by legendary producer Ross Robinson, Ghostemane and Bill Armstrong. Produced by Robinson, the record is a once-in-a-generation debut that bottles the raw charge of a new wave of hardcore punk and features 11 blistering tracks powered by defiance, authenticity and unbridled talent. SQUID PISSER is a chaotic hardcore/noise outfit blending industrial textures, fractured rhythms, and confrontational performance into a singular, abrasive identity. Featuring members of GWAR, CANCER CHRIST and Duck Duck Goose, the band fuses blown-out electronics, noise-drenched guitars, and volatile live energy into something deliberately unhinged and immediate. The band has worked with acclaimed producers including Kurt Ballou and Steve Evetts, and has engaged with forward-thinking acts such as Melt-Banana, The Locust, and Nekrogoblikon. Releases through Three One G Records and Skin Graft Records position SQUID PISSER firmly within a lineage of boundary-pushing underground music.
events.title: The Dillinger Escape Plan - Final Calculating Infinity Shows

events.summary: Skeletons Out of the Closet The annual Spooky Art Show returns to Lavaun's Community Gallery for its third year, this time as “Skeleton's Out of the Closet.” Curated from an open call for submissions, this show features art that is spooky, scary, strange, and out of the ordinary. Alberta Street Gallery member Julia Alora, a lifetime lover of Halloween, has hand-picked this year’s collection of frights and delights from more than 10 local artists. What makes art spooky? Art that focuses on fears, phobias, or disquieting themes. Settings or characters or creatures that are dark, born from night, or upsetting to see. Images that capture the fun and nostalgia of playing in a scary space through a safe lens, reminiscent of horror movies and Halloweens past. Come in for a thrill and a chill, find a new piece to haunt your home, and enjoy beautiful works of art perfect for those who are strange and unusual. Alberta Street Gallery is a friendly and vibrant cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.

events.summary: Get ready for eight days of frightfully fun festivities as Hallo-Week returns to Vancouver Mall, bringing a full lineup of free, family-friendly Halloween celebrations! Finally, Hallo-Week concludes on Saturday, October 31, from 1–5 PM, with Spooktacular Trick-or-Treating, inviting children ages 10 and under to collect candy and goodies from participating retailers throughout the shopping center, while supplies last. events.summary: McMenamins and Oregon Historical Society present History Pub Charismatic religious leaders have long sought to realize their visions in the vast expanses of the American West. American evangelicals who flocked to the once-sleepy mountain town of Colorado Springs planted new churches and built religious empires that left their mark on American politics - including 1990s political campaigns in Oregon. New Age spirituality has made tarot cards, astrology, and crystals ubiquitous. "Mother God," the former leader of the Colorado-based Love Has Won movement, and the mysterious channeler "Ramtha," based in Yelm, Washington, built large and devout followings based on their teachings. Historian Will Schultz and journalist Leah Sottile illuminate how fear, hope, spirituality, and capitalism have been stoked by religious radicals in the American West. Will Schultz is the author of Jesus Springs: Evangelical Capitalism and the Fate of an American City. Leah Sottile is the author of Blazing Eye Sees All: Love Has One, False Profits and the Fever Dream of the American New Age,
events.title: From New Age to Evangelical: Radical Religion in the American West

events.summary: Lloyd Jones is a consummate guitarist/singer/songwriter/arranger/performer/ bandleader. One of the most original artists on the modern day blues scene, Jones is, in the words of Blues Revue, "certainly worthy of greater recognition." The release of his first recording for Blind Pig Records, Love Gotcha, should bring him the national and international acclamation he deserves. Jones was born in Seattle into a musical family, which moved to Portland soon afterward. "I remember music was everywhere in our house growing up. My dad was playing Dixieland jazz records and trying to teach me to play trumpet when I was only five years old. My older brother played drums and showed me how. Then he took me to his band rehearsals and had me playing gigs when I was just 13. He took me to see James Brown in '64. You've got to imagine James in '64 - ouch! Then B.B. King, Buddy Guy, even Sonny Terry and Brownie McGhee - all this before I was out of high school. I was underage and totally mesmerized" Jones got deep into the blues and was the leader of Portland's most popular blues bands, Brown Sugar, in the early 70's. "We got to work with touring musicians in those days, like Charlie Musselwhite, George "Harmonica" Smith, the Johnny Otis show, Big Mama Thornton and Big Walter Horton. That's how we learned, and that's really when I first picked up the guitar. A lot of times these people would stay at our homes and teach us music and history. Some of them have passed now, so I cherish those memories. S.P. Leary, who was in Muddy Waters band and was playing drums with Big Walter at the time, leaned over to me as he was leaving town and said, "Man, I'm getting old. You gotta keep it alive. It's a struggle sometimes, but if you love it, you keep on struggling."' Through the years Jones would continue to hone his craft by performing with the likes of Albert Collins, Robert Cray, Bonnie Raitt, Taj Mahal, B.B. King, Dr. John, John Hammond, Etta James, Junior Wells and Buddy Guy, and many more music legends. In the 80's Jones joined forces with ex-Robert Cray singer/harp player Curtis Salgado in a band called In Yo' Face. "That was one fun band! Seemed like we all had the same record collection. Curtis really pushed me as a guitar player, and when he left in '85 to join Roomful of Blues I knew it was time to play my music." Jones knew what he wanted to say and how he wanted to say it. The Lloyd Jones Struggle started in 1985 as a vehicle for his songwriting. "I love a good story. Most of the traditional blues stayed with a shuffle or slow blues. Being a drummer I keep hearing the rhythm of the words all broke down funky and swamp-afied; nice and relaxed but kind of turned inside out." Jones made two recordings in the late 80's for Criminal Records: The Lloyd Jones Struggle \(1987\) and Small Potatoes \(1989\). They won over a dozen local music awards, as well as acclaim from national music publications such as Down Beat and Guitar Player, which in turn led to some extensive touring for the band on the Miller Beer Sponsorship Program. In 1993 Jones released his third album, Lloyd \`Have Mercy' Jones - Live! on the Burnside Records label. In 1995 Lloyd Jones recorded a highly acclaimed album for the Audio Quest label, entitled Trouble Monkey. Blues Revue named it, "not only one of the best albums of 1995, it is one of the best albums of the 1990's," while Robert Cray called it "the best damn record I've heard in a long time!" Vintage Guitar Magazine said, "Jones offers vocals that would make Sam and Dave smile and guitar work Steve Cropper would be proud of" and referred to his affecting vocals as "gritty as a dirt road and smooth as melting butter." Lloyd's songwriting was starting to be noticed as well, with Joe Louis Walker and Gatemouth Brown covering two of his compositions. Jones and his band have become a mainstay on the West Coast circuit, and have brought their tasteful, crowd-pleasing brand of music from New Orleans to Canada to the Caribbean, where Delbert McClinton witnessed a performance and remarked, "When I heard Lloyd Jones live for the first time in January 1999, it was like exhaling after holding my breath for fifteen years." It was such a typically memorable set at the Santa Cruz Blues Festival that led to Jones' signing by Blind Pig Records. Jones describes his soulful and intelligent fusion of funk, blues, and R&B as "storytelling with a Memphis groove." His latest CD, Love Gotcha, presents Lloyd's writing at its trenchant best. His songs have the quality that makes them sound as if they have been around as blues standards for years or they seem to have fallen out of some time warp from the golden days of R&B. His approach to the guitar is both economical and rhythmically sophisticated, with a style that can be as delicate as it is devastating. And Jones' accomplished guitar and vocal work are complemented throughout the recording by some of the funkiest horn-rhythm-organ arrangements around. Blues lovers everywhere are about to discover what Lloyd Jones' fans already know - one taste of his beguiling music and you're captivated. Lloyd's gotcha! Blind Pig Records A division of Whole Hog, Inc. PO. Box 2344, San Francisco, CA 94126
